  protocol_deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this eligibility criterion assessment resulted in a protocol deviation (i.e., subject enrolled despite not meeting a criterion without an approved waiver). Triggers deviation reporting workflow.']
  protocol_version varchar [note: 'Version of the study protocol under which this eligibility assessment was performed. Critical for audit trail when protocol amendments change inclusion/exclusion criteria.']
  query_open_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an open data discrepancy query exists against this eligibility assessment record in the EDC system. Supports data cleaning status monitoring and DBL readiness tracking.']
  re_screening_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this eligibility assessment is part of a re-screening attempt following an initial screen failure. Supports enrollment funnel analytics and re-screening rate KPI reporting.']
  screen_failure_reason varchar [note: 'Coded or free-text reason for screen failure when the overall eligibility determination is INELIGIBLE. Used for enrollment analytics, site performance reporting, and protocol feasibility review.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'CDISC SDTM domain code for this eligibility assessment record. Always \'IE\' (Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria Not Met) for regulatory submission datasets. Supports SDTM mapping and NDA/BLA/MAA submission.']
  sdtm_sequence_number varchar [note: 'CDISC SDTM sequence number (IESEQ) uniquely identifying this record within the IE domain for a given subject. Required for regulatory submission dataset construction.']
  sdv_date date [note: 'Date on which Source Data Verification (SDV) was completed for this eligibility assessment record by the CRA. Null when SDV has not yet been performed.']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of Source Data Verification (SDV) performed by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) for this eligibility assessment record. Tracks monitoring compliance per the monitoring plan.']
  source_data_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the source document or data entry (e.g., medical record number, lab report ID, physical examination note) that supports the eligibility criterion assessment. Required for Source Data Verification (SDV) by CRA.']
  waiver_approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the sponsor or IRB/IEC approved the protocol exception or waiver for this eligibility criterion. Null when no waiver was requested or waiver was denied.']
  waiver_justification varchar [note: 'Free-text clinical or scientific justification provided by the investigator for requesting a protocol exception or waiver for this eligibility criterion. Required for regulatory audit trail.']
  waiver_requested boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a protocol deviation waiver or exception was requested for this criterion when the subject did not meet it. True when a waiver request has been submitted to the sponsor or IRB/IEC.']
  waiver_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the protocol-specified exception or waiver request for this eligibility criterion. Applicable only when waiver_requested is True. Tracks sponsor or IRB/IEC decision.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of the inclusion/exclusion criteria assessment performed for a subject during screening. Captures each criterion code, criterion text, assessment result (met/not met/not assessed), assessment date, assessor identity, and overall eligibility determination. Tracks waiver requests and protocol-specified exceptions. Provides the audit trail for subject eligibility decisions required by GCP. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC and Oracle Clinical One.'
}

Table subject.subject_contact {
  subject_contact_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the subject contact record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.']

  consent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject has provided explicit consent to be contacted for study-related communications (visit reminders, follow-up calls). True = consent granted; False = consent not granted or withdrawn. Governed by GDPR and HIPAA privacy requirements.']

  contact_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the subject contact record. \'active\' indicates the contact details are current and in use; \'inactive\' indicates superseded or no longer valid; \'withdrawn\' indicates the subject has withdrawn consent for contact; \'pending_verification\' indicates details awaiting confirmation; \'deceased\' indicates the subject is deceased and contact is no longer applicable.']
  country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the subject\'s home address (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Determines applicable data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA) and communication rules.']

  do_not_contact_flag boolean [note: 'Hard stop flag indicating the subject must not be contacted under any circumstances (excluding mandatory safety communications). True = do not contact; False = contact permitted per consent settings. Overrides all other contact preferences.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'Date from which this contact record is considered valid and active. Supports temporal versioning of contact information to maintain a history of address and phone changes over the course of a long-running trial.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'Date on which this contact record ceased to be valid (e.g., subject moved, changed phone number). Null for the currently active record. Enables Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) Type 2 history tracking of contact information.']
  email_address varchar [note: 'Primary email address for the subject. Used for electronic communications including visit reminders, eConsent notifications, and patient engagement via Clinpal.']
  email_consent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject has specifically consented to receive communications via email. True = email contact permitted; False = email contact not permitted. Distinct from general contact consent as email may carry additional regulatory requirements.']
  emergency_contact_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the subject\'s designated emergency contact person. Used by site staff to reach a responsible party in the event of a serious adverse event (SAE) or medical emergency.']
  emergency_contact_phone varchar [note: 'Phone number for the subject\'s emergency contact. Used exclusively for safety-related communications and serious adverse event (SAE) follow-up.']
  emergency_contact_relationship varchar [note: 'Relationship of the emergency contact person to the subject (e.g., spouse, parent, legal guardian). Provides context for site staff when initiating emergency communications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spouse|parent|child|sibling|friend|caregiver|legal_guardian|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  last_contact_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent successful contact with the subject. Used to track subject engagement, identify subjects at risk of dropout, and support visit compliance monitoring.']
  last_contact_method varchar [note: 'Communication channel used during the most recent successful contact with the subject. Supports analysis of effective outreach strategies and visit compliance improvement.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes recorded by site staff regarding the subject\'s contact preferences, special communication instructions, or relevant context (e.g., best time to call, language interpreter required). Classified as confidential due to potential inclusion of sensitive subject information.']
  postal_code varchar [note: 'Postal or ZIP code of the subject\'s home address. Used for geographic analysis, site feasibility, and postal communications.']
  preferred_contact_method varchar [note: 'Subject\'s stated preference for how they wish to be contacted by the site or sponsor. Governs outreach channel selection for visit reminders and safety follow-up. \'no_contact\' indicates the subject has requested no proactive outreach.']
  preferred_contact_time timestamp [note: 'Subject\'s preferred time of day to be contacted. Supports scheduling of outreach calls and reminders to maximize response rates and respect subject preferences.']
  preferred_language varchar [note: 'ISO 639-1/639-2 language code representing the subject\'s preferred language for communications (e.g., \'en\', \'fr\', \'de\', \'zh-CN\'). Ensures communications are delivered in the subject\'s native language to support informed participation.']
  primary_phone varchar [note: 'Primary telephone number for contacting the subject. Used for visit reminders, recruitment follow-up, and safety follow-up communications. Stored in international format where possible.']

  record_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the contact record indicating the role of the contact in relation to the subject. \'primary\' is the subject themselves; \'secondary\' is an alternate contact; \'emergency\' is for emergency use only; \'caregiver\' is a designated caregiver; \'legal_representative\' is a legally authorized representative.']
  safety_contact_override_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether safety-critical communications (e.g., SAE follow-up, urgent safety notifications) are permitted even when do_not_contact_flag is True.   secondary_phone varchar [note: 'Alternate telephone number for the subject, used when the primary phone is unreachable. Supports visit compliance and safety follow-up.']
  secondary_phone_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the secondary phone number (e.g., mobile, home, work).']
  sms_consent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject has specifically consented to receive communications via SMS/text message. True = SMS contact permitted; False = SMS contact not permitted.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which this contact record was sourced. Supports data lineage and reconciliation between Clinpal (eConsent/patient engagement) and Oracle Siebel CTMS (clinical trial management).']
  source_system_contact_key varchar [note: 'Natural key or unique identifier of this contact record in the originating source system (Clinpal or Oracle Siebel CTMS). Enables bidirectional traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the operational system.']
  state_province varchar [note: 'State, province, or region of the subject\'s home address. Supports regulatory reporting and geographic stratification of subject populations.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this subject contact record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles. Tracks when contact details were last updated by site staff.']

  Note: 'Master entity storing contact and communication details for a trial subject, including primary phone, secondary phone, email address, preferred contact method, emergency contact name and relationship, home address (street, city, state, postal code, country), and privacy consent flags for contact. Supports patient recruitment follow-up, visit reminders, and safety follow-up communications. Governed by GDPR and HIPAA data privacy requirements. Sourced from Clinpal and Oracle Siebel CTMS.'

  void_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation for why the payment was voided (e.g., duplicate payment, subject withdrew, incorrect amount, payment returned). Required when void_date is populated.']
  withholding_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Amount withheld from the gross payment for tax purposes (e.g., backup withholding for US subjects who have not provided a valid TIN/SSN). Net payment to subject equals payment_amount minus withholding_amount.']

Distinct from investigator site payments owned by the finance domain. Sourced from Oracle Siebel CTMS and Greenphire ClinCard.'
}

  protocol_version varchar [note: 'The version of the study protocol in effect at the time this medical history record was collected. Ensures traceability of data to the applicable protocol amendment.']
  query_open_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether there is at least one open data query (discrepancy) against this medical history record in the EDC system. Supports data cleaning and database lock readiness tracking.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'The date on which the pre-existing medical condition resolved or ended. Null if the condition is ongoing at the time of assessment. Corresponds to SDTM MHENDTC.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'The CDISC SDTM domain code for this record. For medical history records this is always \'MH\'. Used during SDTM dataset generation for regulatory submissions.']
  sdv_date date [note: 'The date on which source data verification was completed for this medical history record by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA).']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of source data verification for this medical history record. Indicates whether the CRA has verified the eCRF data against source documents at the investigational site.']
  severity varchar [note: 'Clinical severity grading of the pre-existing medical condition as assessed by the investigator. Supports safety profiling and eligibility assessment.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record from which this medical history record was sourced (e.g., Medidata Rave EDC). Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the lakehouse.']
  source_system_record_reference varchar [note: 'The native primary key or record identifier of this medical history entry in the originating source system (e.g., Medidata Rave record OID). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse and the EDC.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this medical history record was last modified in the EDC system or lakehouse. Required for audit trail compliance and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.']

  Note: 'Records subject medical history and pre-existing conditions collected during screening, coded to MedDRA terms, with onset dates, resolution status, and relevance to study eligibility.'
}

Table subject.visit_billing_reconciliation {
  visit_billing_reconciliation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the visit_billing_reconciliation association']
  invoice_line_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the sponsor invoice line item under which this subject visit is being billed.']
  subject_visit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the subject visit record being reconciled against a sponsor invoice line.']
  billing_period_end date [note: 'The end date of the billing period during which this subject visit was included in the invoice line. Together with billing_period_start, defines the billing window for this reconciliation record.']
  billing_period_start date [note: 'The start date of the billing period during which this subject visit was included in the invoice line. Belongs to the reconciliation relationship as it defines the temporal scope of this specific visit-to-line billing association.']
  billing_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the billing reconciliation for this subject visit against this invoice line. Tracks the lifecycle of the billing event from initial inclusion through dispute resolution and final reconciliation. Belongs to the relationship, not to either entity alone.']
  quantity_billed decimal [note: 'The number of visit units attributed to this subject_visit on this invoice_line. Belongs to the reconciliation relationship as it represents the billing quantity allocated to this specific visit-line pairing, which may differ from the invoice_line.quantity aggregate.']
  subject_count varchar [note: 'Number of clinical trial subjects (patients) associated with this billing line item, applicable for per-patient billing milestones such as enrollment, randomization, or completion fees. [Moved from invoice_line: subject_count on invoice_line is an aggregate count of subjects associated with a billing line — this aggregate is derivable from COUNT(*) on visit_billing_reconciliation grouped by invoice_line_id. Storing it as a denormalized integer on invoice_line creates a maintenance burden and risks inconsistency. It should be removed from invoice_line and computed from the association table.]']
  visit_completion_date date [note: 'The date the subject visit was confirmed complete and eligible for billing reconciliation against this invoice line. Belongs to the reconciliation relationship, not to the visit record alone, as the billing-eligible completion date may differ from the actual_visit_date due to SDV or query resolution timing.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the billing reconciliation event between a subject_visit and an invoice_line in clinical trials sponsor invoicing. It captures the operational linkage used by finance teams to reconcile per-visit billing charges on sponsor invoices against actual subject visit completions. Each record links one subject_visit to one invoice_line and carries the billing period, quantity billed, completion date, and billing status that exist only in the context of this reconciliation relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials sponsor billing, invoice lines are aggregated billing records that cover multiple subject visits of a given type (e.g., all Week 4 visits at a site in a billing period), meaning one invoice_line maps to many subject_visits. Conversely, a given subject_visit type can be billed across multiple invoice lines in different billing periods or contract amendments, meaning one subject_visit can be referenced by multiple invoice_lines. The clinical trials finance team actively manages this reconciliation — tracking which visits have been billed, in which period, at what quantity — as a core operational process for sponsor invoicing accuracy and audit support.'
}

Table subject.sdv_review {
  sdv_review_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the sdv_review association']
  subject_visit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the subject visit that was reviewed during this SDV review event.']
  review_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the CRA performed SDV for this subject visit during this monitoring visit. Distinct from the monitoring visit actual_start_date as SDV may span multiple days.']
  review_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this SDV review record. Drives follow-up actions and monitoring report completeness checks.']
  sdv_coverage_percent decimal [note: 'Percentage of data points or CRF fields within this subject visit that were verified during this monitoring visit. Belongs to the review pair, not to either entity alone.']
  sdv_date date [note: 'Date on which Source Data Verification (SDV) was completed for this visit by the assigned CRA. Null if SDV has not been completed. Used for monitoring compliance reporting. [Moved from subject_visit: sdv_date on subject_visit represents the date of a specific SDV review event. When re-SDV occurs across multiple monitoring visits, a single sdv_date on subject_visit loses historical review date information. This attribute belongs to the sdv_review association as review_date, preserving the full SDV review history per pair.]']
  sdv_outcome varchar [note: 'Result of the SDV review for this subject visit during this monitoring visit. Captures whether data was verified clean, discrepancies were found, or verification was not possible.']
  sdv_performed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether Source Data Verification was actually conducted for this subject visit during this monitoring visit. False indicates the subject visit was in scope but SDV was not completed (e.g., source documents unavailable).']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of Source Data Verification (SDV) for this visit, indicating whether the CRA has verified the eCRF data against source documents. Drives monitoring visit planning and risk-based monitoring decisions. [Moved from subject_visit: sdv_status on subject_visit represents the outcome of a specific SDV review event conducted during a specific monitoring visit. When a subject visit is reviewed across multiple monitoring visits (re-SDV), a single sdv_status on subject_visit cannot represent all review outcomes. This attribute belongs to the sdv_review association where it is captured per monitoring-visit/subject-visit pair as review_status.]']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Source Data Verification (SDV) Review event between a subject_visit and a monitoring_visit. It captures the operational record of a CRA reviewing a specific subject visit during a specific monitoring visit, including SDV outcome, coverage percentage, review date, and review status. Each record links one subject_visit to one monitoring_visit and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this review pairing — a subject visit may be reviewed across multiple monitoring visits (re-SDV, follow-up), and a monitoring visit covers many subject visits.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a CRA monitoring visit (monitoring_visit) covers SDV across multiple enrolled subjects and their corresponding subject visits — a single monitoring visit reviews many subject visits. Conversely, a single subject visit can be reviewed across multiple monitoring visits over the study lifecycle (initial SDV, re-SDV, follow-up verification after queries). The business actively tracks SDV outcome, coverage percentage, and review status per subject-visit/monitoring-visit pair as an operational record, not a derived analytical correlation.'
}

Table subject.subject_subject_consent {
  subject_consent_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the subject_consent association']

  consent_status varchar [note: 'Current status of this specific consent signing event. A subject may have a signed status for an earlier ICF version and a pending status for a newer version requiring re-consent. Belongs to the individual consent event record.']
  icf_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject signed the most recent version of the Informed Consent Form (ICF). Must precede any study-related screening procedures. Used for GCP compliance verification and regulatory inspection readiness. [Moved from trial_subject: icf_date on trial_subject captures only the most recent consent date and cannot represent the full re-consent history. This date belongs to each individual consent signing event and should live on the subject_consent association, where one record per signing event captures the date accurately.]']
  icf_signed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject has signed a valid Informed Consent Form (ICF) prior to any study-related procedures. Mandatory regulatory requirement. True = ICF signed and on file; False = ICF not yet signed or consent withdrawn. Sourced from Clinpal eConsent or site paper ICF records. [Moved from trial_subject: This BOOLEAN on trial_subject is a derived/summary flag indicating whether any valid ICF has been signed. It can be computed from the subject_consent association (any record with consent_status = signed). Storing it on trial_subject creates a maintenance burden and potential inconsistency. It may be retained as a computed/derived attribute but should not be the source of truth.]']
  icf_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the Informed Consent Form signed by the subject. Tracks which IRB/IEC-approved consent version was used. Critical for re-consent tracking when protocol amendments require updated ICF versions. [Moved from trial_subject: icf_version on trial_subject is a denormalized scalar that captures only the latest ICF version signed. It is replaced by the FK document_icf_version_id on the subject_consent association, which properly links to the document_icf_version master and supports full consent history. This attribute should be removed from trial_subject.]']
  reconsent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this consent event was a re-consent (true) due to a protocol amendment or new safety information, or an initial consent (false) at enrollment. Belongs to the signing event, not to the subject or the ICF version.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Informed Consent Event between a trial_subject and a document_icf_version. It captures the complete regulatory audit trail of every consent and re-consent signing event for each subject across all ICF versions applicable during their participation in the study. Each record links one trial_subject to one document_icf_version and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific signing event — including the date, method, status, and witness. Required for regulatory inspection readiness and TMF completeness.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a subject signs an ICF at initial enrollment and must re-consent whenever a protocol amendment produces a new ICF version — meaning one subject can sign multiple ICF versions over the life of a trial. Conversely, each ICF version is signed by many subjects (all those enrolled or re-consented under that version). The business actively manages these consent records as a regulatory and compliance obligation, tracking the date, method, and status of each individual consent event.'
}

Table subject.drug_lab_interaction {
  drug_lab_interaction_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the drug_lab_interaction association']
  assessor_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the employee (clinician, medical monitor, or data manager) who performed the drug-lab interaction assessment and documented the linkage. Belongs to the relationship as it identifies who made the specific clinical judgment connecting this lab result to this medication record.']
  concomitant_medication_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the concomitant medication record whose initiation, dose change, or discontinuation was driven by the associated laboratory finding.']
  lab_result_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the laboratory result that triggered or informed the concomitant medication decision.']
  assessment_date date [note: 'The date on which the clinical assessment was performed connecting the laboratory result to the medication action. Belongs to the relationship as it records when the linkage was evaluated, independent of the lab result date or medication start/stop dates.']
  clinical_rationale varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded clinical justification provided by the assessor explaining the causal or correlative link between the laboratory finding and the medication decision. Belongs to the relationship, not to either entity alone.']
  trigger_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the type of medication action that was triggered or informed by the associated laboratory result. Belongs to the relationship because the same medication record may be initiated for one lab result and dose-reduced for another.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the clinical assessment event linking a concomitant medication record to a laboratory result that triggered or informed a medication decision. It captures the pharmacovigilance and drug-lab interaction relationship between a specific medication action (initiation, dose change, or discontinuation) and the laboratory finding(s) that drove that clinical decision. Each record links one concomitant_medication to one lab_result with attributes that exist only in the context of this assessed relationship, supporting safety monitoring, regulatory reporting, and SDTM CM-LB linkage.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, concomitant medications are frequently initiated, modified, or discontinued in direct response to laboratory findings — a statin started after elevated LDL, a dose reduction triggered by elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST), or a medication stopped due to a critical creatinine value. One abnormal lab result can trigger multiple medication adjustments (e.g., both a diuretic dose reduction AND a potassium supplement initiation), and one medication change can be supported by multiple lab results reviewed together (e.g., a series of rising LFT values). This is an operationally managed relationship in pharmacovigilance and drug-lab interaction safety review workflows.'
}

  is_susar boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this adverse event has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited regulatory reporting to health authorities (FDA, EMA, MHRA, etc.) within defined timelines (7 or 15 calendar days).']
  is_teae boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the adverse event is treatment-emergent, defined as an event that first occurred or worsened in severity after the first dose of investigational product. Used in TEAE incidence tables in the CSR and SAP-defined safety analyses.']
  meddra_llt_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) numeric code assigned during medical coding, representing the most granular level of the MedDRA hierarchy closest to the verbatim term.']
  meddra_llt_name varchar [note: 'MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) text description corresponding to the LLT code. Used in safety listings, narratives, and regulatory submissions.']
  meddra_pt_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) numeric code, the primary level used for regulatory reporting, signal detection, and aggregate safety analysis.']
  meddra_pt_name varchar [note: 'MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) text description. The standardized medical term used in all regulatory submissions, DSMB/DMC reports, and safety narratives.']
  meddra_soc_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) numeric code representing the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for aggregate safety tabulations by body system in CSRs and regulatory submissions.']
  meddra_soc_name varchar [note: 'MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) text description. Used in safety tabulations, listings, and figures in the Clinical Study Report (CSR).']
  meddra_version varchar [note: 'Version of the MedDRA dictionary used for coding this adverse event (e.g., \'26.0\'). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coded terms across dictionary versions.']
  medical_history_related boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the adverse event is considered related to or a continuation of a pre-existing medical history condition, as assessed by the investigator. Supports pre-existing condition confounding analysis.']
  narrative varchar [note: 'Free-text medical narrative describing the clinical course of the adverse event, including relevant medical history, treatment, and outcome. Required for SAE/SUSAR regulatory submissions and DSMB/DMC safety reviews.']
  onset_date date [note: 'The date on which the adverse event first began, as reported by the investigator. This is the principal real-world event date used for duration calculations, expedited reporting timelines, and TEAE determination.']
  outcome varchar [note: 'Final or current outcome of the adverse event as assessed by the investigator. Used in safety listings, aggregate safety tables, and regulatory submissions.']
  regulatory_report_due_date date [note: 'The deadline by which an expedited safety report (e.g., SUSAR, IND Safety Report) must be submitted to the relevant health authority. Calculated from the date of first awareness per ICH E2A timelines (7-day for fatal/life-threatening, 15-day for other SUSARs).']
  regulatory_report_submitted_date date [note: 'The actual date on which the expedited safety report was submitted to the health authority. Used to calculate compliance with regulatory reporting timelines and track submission performance KPIs.']
  report_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this record represents the initial AE report, a follow-up update with new clinical information, or the final report upon event resolution. Supports version history tracking as the clinical picture evolves.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'The date on which the adverse event resolved or returned to baseline. Null if the event is ongoing. Used to calculate AE duration and determine outcome status.']
  seriousness_criteria varchar [note: 'Specific ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by this SAE (e.g., death, life-threatening, hospitalization required, persistent disability, congenital anomaly, medically significant). Multiple criteria may apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]']
  severity varchar [note: 'Descriptive severity classification of the adverse event as assessed by the investigator (mild, moderate, severe, life-threatening, fatal). Distinct from CTCAE grade; used in non-oncology studies and as a complementary severity descriptor per ICH E2A.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this adverse event record was sourced (Oracle Argus Safety, Medidata Rave EDC, Oracle Clinical One, or manual entry). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements.']
  study_day_onset varchar [note: 'The study day (relative to first dose date) on which the adverse event began. Calculated per CDISC convention (Day 1 = first dose date). Used in time-to-event analyses and safety exposure-adjusted incidence calculations.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this adverse event record was most recently modified in the source system. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential version number of this AE record, incremented with each follow-up update. Version 1 is the initial report; subsequent versions capture evolving clinical information. Enables temporal evolution tracking across the AE lifecycle.']

  Note: 'Core master record for every adverse event (AE) reported during a clinical trial, capturing onset date, resolution date, severity grade per CTCAE, seriousness flag, expectedness, relationship to investigational product, action taken, outcome, and follow-up version history. Each AE may progress through multiple follow-up updates as clinical picture evolves, with version tracking for each update. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety and EDC (Medidata Rave). This is the SSOT for all AE occurrences and their temporal evolution across studies and subjects.'
}

  pt_code varchar [note: 'Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the Preferred Term (PT) to which the LLT maps. The PT is the primary level used for regulatory reporting, safety queries, and signal detection. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety.']
  pt_name varchar [note: 'Descriptive text of the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) corresponding to pt_code. Used as the standard term in regulatory submissions, CIOMS forms, and safety narratives.']
  recoding_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text justification provided by the coder when a previously assigned MedDRA code is revised (coding_method = \'recoded\'). Required for audit trail integrity and regulatory inspection readiness. Null when coding_method is not \'recoded\'.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp at which this MedDRA coding record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp at which this MedDRA coding record was last modified in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Tracks the most recent update for change detection, incremental processing, and audit trail compliance.']
  soc_code varchar [note: 'Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the System Organ Class (SOC), the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy. SOC is the primary axis for organizing adverse events in regulatory safety tables (e.g., Table 14.3.1 in ICH E3 CSR).']
  soc_name varchar [note: 'Descriptive text of the MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) corresponding to soc_code. Used as the primary grouping header in all regulatory safety tabulations, PSUR/PBRER narratives, and DSMB reports.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system from which this MedDRA coding record was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer. Typically \'argus_safety\' for records originating from Oracle Argus Safety.']
  verbatim_term varchar [note: 'The exact, unmodified adverse event term as reported by the investigator or subject in the source document or eCRF prior to MedDRA coding. Preserved for ALCOA+ compliance and audit trail. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety verbatim field.']

  Note: 'Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) — the annual periodic safety report submitted to health authorities summarizing cumulative safety data for an investigational product across all ongoing studies.   is_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this CTCAE grade definition record is currently active and available for use in new AE grading assignments.   hlgt_code varchar [note: 'The 8-digit MedDRA code for the High Level Group Term (HLGT) in the primary SOC path for this term. Populated for LLT, PT, HLT, and HLGT level terms to support aggregate safety analysis and regulatory tabulations at the HLGT level.']

  is_primary_soc boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this term\'s association to a System Organ Class (SOC) is the primary (true) or secondary (false) SOC linkage.   language_code varchar [note: 'ISO 639-1/639-2 language code for the language of this term record (e.g., \'en\' for English, \'ja\' for Japanese, \'de\' for German).   llt_code varchar [note: 'The 8-digit MedDRA code for the Lowest Level Term (LLT). For LLT-level records this equals term_code. For higher-level terms this field is null.   llt_name varchar [note: 'The official MedDRA name of the Lowest Level Term (LLT). For LLT-level records this equals term_name. Null for higher-level terms. Used in verbatim coding workflows and auto-coding dictionaries in Oracle Argus Safety.']

  meddra_version varchar [note: 'The biannual MedDRA release version in which this term was introduced or last updated (e.g., \'27.0\', \'26.1\'). Critical for regulatory submissions requiring version-specific coding, database lock (DBL) documentation, and CDISC SDTM dataset compliance. MedDRA releases occur twice yearly (March and September).']
  pt_code varchar [note: 'The 8-digit MedDRA code for the Preferred Term (PT) to which this term maps. For PT-level records this equals term_code. For LLT-level records this is the parent PT code.   pt_name varchar [note: 'The official MedDRA name of the Preferred Term (PT) to which this term maps. Denormalized for direct use in adverse event coding displays, safety narratives, CDISC SDTM datasets, and regulatory submissions without requiring a hierarchy join.']
  rave_dict_entry_reference varchar [note: 'The dictionary entry identifier assigned by Medidata Rave EDC when this MedDRA term is configured in the Rave coding dictionary for eCRF verbatim-to-MedDRA auto-coding.   replacement_term_code varchar [note: 'The 8-digit MedDRA code of the term that replaces this term when it has been retired, split, or merged.   retired_version varchar [note: 'The MedDRA version in which this term was retired, if applicable. Null for active terms. Used to enforce coding rules in Oracle Argus Safety and to flag terms that should not be applied to new adverse event records after the specified version.']
  retirement_date date [note: 'The date on which this MedDRA term was officially retired by MSSO, corresponding to the release date of the version in which it was retired. Null for active terms. Used to enforce coding restrictions in Oracle Argus Safety and to flag terms in legacy study datasets.']
  smq_membership varchar [note: 'Pipe-delimited list of Standardised MedDRA Query (SMQ) names to which this PT belongs. SMQs are validated, topic-focused groupings of MedDRA terms used for signal detection, aggregate safety analysis, and regulatory queries (e.g., \'Anaphylactic reaction\', \'Drug-induced liver injury\'). Populated for PT-level terms only.']
  smq_scope varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this term\'s SMQ membership is classified as \'broad\' (higher sensitivity, more inclusive) or \'narrow\' (higher specificity, more restrictive) within the associated SMQ.   soc_abbreviation varchar [note: 'The standardized two-to-four letter abbreviation for the System Organ Class (SOC) as defined by MSSO (e.g., \'CARD\' for Cardiac disorders, \'NERV\' for Nervous system disorders).   soc_code varchar [note: 'The 8-digit MedDRA code for the System Organ Class (SOC) to which this term is linked (primary or secondary).   soc_name varchar [note: 'The official MedDRA name of the System Organ Class (SOC) associated with this term. Denormalized for direct use in safety tabulations, DSMB/DMC reports, and CDISC SDTM datasets (AEBODSYS variable) without requiring a hierarchy join.']
  source_file_name varchar [note: 'The name of the MSSO-distributed MedDRA ASCII flat file from which this term record was loaded (e.g., \'llt.asc\', \'pt.asc\', \'hlt.asc\', \'hlgt.asc\', \'soc.asc\').   term_code varchar [note: 'The official 8-digit numeric MedDRA term code assigned by the Maintenance and Support Services Organization (MSSO) uniquely identifying this term within the MedDRA hierarchy.   term_name varchar [note: 'The official MedDRA term label as published by MSSO for this term code. Represents the standardized medical concept name used in adverse event coding, regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA), and safety signal detection across all five hierarchy levels.']
  term_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the MedDRA term is currently active and available for coding or has been retired in a subsequent MedDRA version release. Retired terms are retained for historical traceability of previously coded adverse events but must not be used for new coding in Oracle Argus Safety.']
  term_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the term as \'standard\' (fully endorsed MedDRA term) or \'non-standard\' (a term that has been superseded, split, or merged and retained for backward compatibility).   updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this MedDRA term record was last updated in the lakehouse silver layer, typically triggered by a biannual MedDRA version release load. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.']
  who_art_mapping varchar [note: 'The corresponding WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology (WHO-ART) preferred term code or name for this MedDRA term, where a legacy mapping exists.   Note: 'Reference master for the MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) terminology hierarchy, storing all active terms across all five levels: LLT (Lowest Level Term), PT (Preferred Term), HLT (High Level Term), HLGT (High Level Group Term), and SOC (System Organ Class).   quorum_requirement varchar [note: 'Minimum number of committee members required to be present for a meeting to be valid and for decisions to be binding, as specified in the charter. Enforced during meeting scheduling and minutes review.']
  regulatory_authority_notified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA) has been formally notified of the committee\'s establishment and composition, as required for certain study types and jurisdictions.']
  reporting_authority varchar [note: 'Name or role of the organizational body or individual to whom the committee formally reports its recommendations (e.g., \'Sponsor Medical Officer\', \'Executive Steering Committee\', \'IRB/IEC\'). Defines the escalation path for safety recommendations.']

  sponsor_liaison_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the sponsor\'s designated liaison or medical monitor who serves as the primary point of contact between the sponsor organization and the committee. This individual typically attends open sessions but is excluded from closed sessions.']
  statistical_charter_included boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the committee charter includes a statistical analysis plan (SAP) or statistical charter defining interim analysis rules, stopping boundaries (e.g., O\'Brien-Fleming, Lan-DeMets), and alpha-spending functions. Critical for DSMB/DMC oversight of adaptive trials.']
  stopping_rules_defined boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the charter defines pre-specified stopping rules for efficacy, futility, or safety that the committee is empowered to invoke. Presence of stopping rules is a key regulatory expectation for DSMB/DMC charters.']
  tmf_section_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the TMF section or zone in Veeva Vault eTMF where committee-related documents (charter, member CVs, meeting minutes, recommendations) are filed. Aligns with the DIA Reference Model for TMF structure.']

  unblinded_access boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the committee has access to unblinded (treatment-arm-identified) safety and efficacy data during its reviews.   updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this committee record in the lakehouse silver layer. Required for change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.']

  Note: 'Master record for internal sponsor Safety Review Committees (SRCs) and external Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs) overseeing study safety.   updated_meddra_soc_name varchar [note: 'Revised MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) name corresponding to the updated SOC code assigned in this follow-up.']
  updated_outcome varchar [note: 'Revised outcome status of the adverse event as reported in this follow-up, reflecting the subject\'s current clinical condition relative to the event.']
  updated_seriousness_criteria varchar [note: 'Revised seriousness criteria met by the adverse event as of this follow-up (e.g., death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, medically significant). May be a pipe-delimited list of applicable criteria. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]']
  updated_severity varchar [note: 'Updated narrative severity classification of the adverse event as assessed at the time of this follow-up, aligned with ICH E2A severity definitions.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this follow-up record was last modified in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing follow-up information updates for an adverse event after the initial report, including updated severity grade, new causality assessment, additional clinical details, outcome update, and resolution date. Each AE may have multiple follow-up records as the clinical picture evolves. Drives follow-up ICSR submissions in Oracle Argus Safety.'

Table safety.signal_case_contribution {
  signal_case_contribution_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the signal_case_contribution association']
  adverse_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the contributing adverse event case record in the safety domain.']
  signal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the safety signal to which this adverse event case contributes evidence.']
  case_included_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this adverse event case is actively included in the current signal evaluation case pool. Cases may be excluded from a signal\'s active case count due to duplicate detection, data quality issues, or adjudication decisions.']
  case_weight decimal [note: 'Statistical weight assigned to this adverse event case in the context of its contribution to the signal\'s disproportionality metric calculation (e.g., PRR, ROR, BCPNN). Reflects the relative influence of this case on the signal strength value.']
  contribution_date date [note: 'Date on which this adverse event case was formally linked to the safety signal as a contributing case, typically recorded during a signal detection or evaluation cycle run in Oracle Argus Safety.']
  included_in_case_count boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this adverse event case is counted in the safety signal\'s reported case_count denominator. Distinct from case_included_flag — a case may be included in evaluation but excluded from the formal case count due to adjudication or deduplication.']
  signal_detection_cycle varchar [note: 'Identifier for the signal detection or evaluation cycle during which this case-signal contribution was established or last reviewed (e.g., \'Q1-2024\', \'Cycle-7\'). Supports tracking of case pool evolution across multiple evaluation cycles.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Signal Case Contribution event between adverse_event and safety_signal. It captures the formal pharmacovigilance process by which individual adverse event case reports are linked to safety signals as contributing evidence, tracking when each case was included, its statistical weight, and its inclusion status across evaluation cycles. Each record links one adverse_event to one safety_signal with attributes that exist only in the context of this case-to-signal contribution relationship, as governed by ICH E2E and implemented in Oracle Argus Safety.. Existence Justification: In clinical pharmacovigilance, safety signal detection is explicitly an aggregation process where multiple individual adverse event cases (ICSRs) contribute evidence to a single safety signal, and a single adverse event case can contribute to multiple signals (e.g., a hepatotoxicity AE may contribute to both a \'liver injury\' signal and a \'drug-induced liver disease\' signal). This is a formally recognized operational process governed by ICH E2E and implemented in Oracle Argus Safety, where pharmacovigilance teams actively manage which cases are included in each signal evaluation cycle. The relationship itself carries operationally meaningful data: when the case was included, whether it was flagged as contributing, which detection cycle it belongs to, and its statistical weight — none of which belong on the AE record or the signal record alone.'
}

Table safety.dsur_line_listing {
  dsur_line_listing_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the dsur_line_listing association']
  dsur_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Development Safety Update Report in which this SUSAR is listed.']
  susar_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific SUSAR case included in this DSUR line listing.']
  cumulative_vs_period_flag varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this SUSAR contributes to the period count, the cumulative count, or both within the DSUR aggregate summaries. Drives reconciliation between period_susar_count and cumulative_susar_count on the parent DSUR.']
  is_follow_up_in_period boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SUSAR record represents a follow-up submission (not the initial report) that was submitted during this DSUR reporting period. A SUSAR may appear in multiple DSURs — once as initial and again as follow-up.']
  is_new_in_period boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SUSAR first became reportable (awareness date falls within the DSUR reporting period). Used to populate the period_susar_count on the parent DSUR.']
  line_listing_section varchar [note: 'The specific regulatory section of the DSUR document in which this SUSAR appears. ICH E2F requires separate line listings for fatal, serious non-fatal, and unexpected reactions. Determines placement in the final DSUR document.']
  reporting_period_inclusion_type varchar [note: 'Classifies how this SUSAR is included in the DSUR — whether it is a new case first reported during this annual period, a cumulative carry-forward from a prior period, or a case that spans the reporting period boundary. Drives which aggregate count columns in the DSUR are incremented.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory inclusion of a SUSAR within a specific Development Safety Update Report (DSUR). It captures the ICH E2F-mandated line listing relationship between a periodic safety report and individual SUSAR cases, recording whether each case is new in the reporting period or a cumulative carry-forward, which line listing section it appears in, and how it contributes to the DSUR\'s aggregate counts. Each record links one DSUR to one SUSAR with attributes that exist only in the context of this regulatory inclusion decision. Sourced from Oracle Argus Safety periodic reporting module line listing outputs.. Existence Justification: ICH E2F guidelines mandate that DSURs include explicit line listings of all SUSARs occurring during the reporting period AND cumulative summaries across all periods. A single DSUR covers multiple SUSARs (all cases in the reporting period), and a single SUSAR can appear in multiple DSURs (e.g., initial report in one DSUR, follow-up in the next annual period). This is an operationally managed regulatory artifact — safety teams actively curate which SUSARs are included in each DSUR, whether they are new in the period or carry over cumulatively, and in which line listing section they appear.'
}

It captures the operational record of a specific safety signal being reported to a specific health authority, including submission details, authority-specific required actions, and response tracking. Each record links one safety_signal to one health_authority and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific notification — they cannot reside on the signal master record (which is authority-agnostic) nor on the health authority reference record (which is signal-agnostic).. Existence Justification: In clinical trials pharmacovigilance, a single safety signal (e.g., potential hepatotoxicity detected via disproportionality analysis) must be reported to multiple health authorities simultaneously — FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA — each with its own notification deadline, submission reference, and response tracking. Conversely, each health authority receives and tracks many safety signals across all studies and sponsors. The business actively manages these notifications as operational records: safety teams create them, update their status, record agency responses, and audit them for regulatory compliance. This is a textbook operational M:N with rich relationship-specific data.'
}

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory submission event between a SUSAR case and a specific health authority. Each record documents one submission event linking one SUSAR to one health authority, enabling pharmacovigilance teams to track multi-jurisdictional reporting compliance under ICH E2A/E2B obligations.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single SUSAR must be reported simultaneously to multiple health authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA, national competent authorities) under ICH E2A/E2B regulations, each with jurisdiction-specific deadlines, submission formats, and acknowledgement tracking. Conversely, each health authority receives SUSARs from many different studies and cases. The business actively manages each SUSAR-to-authority submission as a distinct operational record with its own submission date, deadline, status, and acknowledgement number — this is not derivable from either entity alone.'

Table safety.assessment_dataset_evidence {

  benefit_risk_assessment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the benefit-risk assessment that this dataset evidence record supports']
  sdtm_dataset_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the SDTM dataset that served as an evidence source for the benefit-risk assessment']
  analysis_population varchar [note: 'The clinical analysis population subset from this SDTM dataset that was used in this benefit-risk assessment (e.g., Intent-to-Treat, Per-Protocol, Safety population).   data_cut_date date [note: 'The specific clinical data cut-off date at which this SDTM dataset\'s data was extracted and used for this particular benefit-risk assessment. May differ from the dataset\'s own generation date if the dataset was regenerated after the assessment was conducted.']

  inclusion_rationale varchar [note: 'Narrative justification for why this specific SDTM dataset was included as an evidence source in this benefit-risk assessment. Documents the scientific and regulatory reasoning, supporting audit trail requirements for regulatory submissions.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Evidence Role relationship between a benefit_risk_assessment and an sdtm_dataset. Each record links one benefit_risk_assessment to one sdtm_dataset and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this specific assessment-dataset pairing.. Existence Justification: In clinical research, a formal benefit-risk assessment (BRA) draws on multiple SDTM datasets simultaneously — for example, a single BRA may reference the AE dataset for safety events, the EX dataset for exposure, and the ADRS/RS dataset for efficacy endpoints. Conversely, a single SDTM dataset (e.g., the AE dataset) will inform multiple BRAs across development phases, periodic reviews, and regulatory requests. The business actively manages which datasets were used in each assessment, including the specific data cut date applied and the role each dataset played (safety evidence, efficacy evidence, exposure quantification), making this a genuine operational M:N relationship with its own attributes.'
}

  dbl_included boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this coding assignment was included in the final database lock (DBL) snapshot for regulatory submission. True = included in DBL; False = excluded or post-lock amendment. Critical for submission integrity and audit trail.']
  dictionary_version varchar [note: 'The specific version of the coding dictionary applied at the time of coding (e.g., MedDRA 26.1, WHO-DD March 2024). Regulatory submissions require explicit dictionary version documentation to ensure reproducibility and consistency.']
  field_name varchar [note: 'The specific eCRF field name within the form from which the verbatim term was captured (e.g., \'AETERM\', \'CMTRT\'). Enables precise source data traceability per ALCOA+ and SDTM variable mapping.']
  form_name varchar [note: 'The name of the eCRF form (e.g., \'Adverse Events\', \'Concomitant Medications\') in Medidata Rave from which the verbatim term was collected. Supports data lineage and source data verification (SDV) traceability.']
  high_level_group_term varchar [note: 'The MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) associated with the assigned Preferred Term. Second-highest level in the MedDRA hierarchy, used for broader safety signal grouping and regulatory tabulations.']
  high_level_term varchar [note: 'The MedDRA High Level Term (HLT) grouping the assigned Preferred Term. Intermediate level in the MedDRA hierarchy between PT and HLGT, used in aggregate safety analyses and signal detection.']
  is_primary_soc boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this coding assignment uses the primary SOC classification for the assigned Preferred Term. MedDRA allows a PT to belong to multiple SOCs; the primary SOC is used for regulatory safety tabulations. True = primary SOC; False = secondary SOC.']
  is_serious_ae boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the verbatim term being coded is associated with a Serious Adverse Event (SAE). True = the source record is an SAE. Drives expedited regulatory reporting timelines (e.g., 7-day/15-day reporting per ICH E2A) and SUSAR assessment workflows.']
  lowest_level_term varchar [note: 'The MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) that most closely matches the verbatim term. The LLT is the most granular level of the MedDRA hierarchy and is used to capture the precise clinical concept before mapping to the PT.']
  medical_review_date date [note: 'The date on which the medical reviewer completed their review of the coding assignment. Null if medical review is not required or not yet performed for this record.']
  preferred_term varchar [note: 'The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) or WHO-DD preferred drug name assigned to the verbatim term. The PT is the primary level of the MedDRA hierarchy used in regulatory safety reporting and aggregate analyses.']
  prior_assigned_code varchar [note: 'The dictionary code that was previously assigned before a recoding event. Preserved for audit trail purposes to document the history of coding changes per ALCOA+ and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements. Null for initial coding assignments.']
  prior_preferred_term varchar [note: 'The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) that was previously assigned before a recoding event. Preserved alongside prior_assigned_code for complete audit trail documentation of coding history changes.']
  pt_code varchar [note: 'The numeric MedDRA code for the Preferred Term (PT). Used in SDTM datasets (AEPTCD) and regulatory submissions. Distinct from the PT text label to support code-based lookups and dictionary version migrations.']
  recoding_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text justification provided by the coder when a previously approved coding assignment is revised (recoded). Required for audit trail integrity and regulatory inspection readiness. Null for initial coding assignments.']
  sdtm_variable varchar [note: 'The CDISC SDTM variable name to which this coding assignment maps (e.g., AEDECOD for AE Preferred Term, AEBODSYS for AE SOC, CMDECOD for CM decoded name). Supports automated SDTM dataset generation and regulatory submission preparation.']
  soc_code varchar [note: 'The numeric MedDRA code for the System Organ Class (SOC). Used in SDTM datasets (AESOCCD) and regulatory submissions to uniquely identify the SOC category.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record from which this coding assignment originated (e.g., Medidata Rave EDC coding module). Supports data lineage tracking and cross-system reconciliation.']
  system_organ_class varchar [note: 'The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) associated with the assigned Preferred Term. The SOC is the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy and is used for aggregate safety tabulations in clinical study reports and regulatory submissions.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this coding assignment record was last modified in the source system. Supports change detection, incremental ETL processing, and ALCOA+ audit trail requirements.']
  verbatim_term varchar [note: 'The exact, unmodified text as entered by the investigator or site staff in the eCRF prior to coding. Preserved verbatim per ALCOA+ principles to maintain data integrity and auditability. May contain patient-reported or clinician-reported language.']
  visit_name varchar [note: 'The name or label of the study visit during which the verbatim term was collected (e.g., \'Screening\', \'Week 4\', \'End of Treatment\'). Provides temporal context for the coded term within the study schedule.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of medical coding assignments applied to verbatim terms collected in eCRFs. Captures verbatim term, coding dictionary (MedDRA or WHO-DD), dictionary version, assigned code, preferred term (PT), system organ class (SOC), lowest level term (LLT), coding method (autocoding, manual), coder user ID, coding date, approval status, and coding flag. Supports regulatory-grade medical coding workflows.'
}

  sdv_user_identifier varchar [note: 'Identifier of the CRA or authorized user who performed Source Data Verification for this audit entry. Provides attribution for the SDV action per GCP monitoring requirements.']

  user_role varchar [note: 'Role of the EDC user at the time of the data change (e.g., CRC - Clinical Research Coordinator, CRA - Clinical Research Associate, PI - Principal Investigator, DATA_MANAGER).   visit_name varchar [note: 'Name of the study visit (e.g., Screening, Week 4, End of Treatment) associated with the eCRF record that was modified. Contextualizes the data change within the study schedule of events.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing ALCOA+ compliance audit trail entries for every clinical data change in the EDC system. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBMETHOD. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: venipuncture|fingerstick|catheter|lumbar_puncture|biopsy|swab|urine_void|other — promote to reference product]']
  collection_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for this specimen collection event, typically generated by the EDC or CTMS (e.g., \'SC-0042-001\'). Used for cross-system traceability and chain-of-custody documentation.']
  collection_site_anatomy varchar [note: 'The anatomical location on the subject\'s body from which the specimen was collected (e.g., \'Left Antecubital Vein\', \'Right Arm\', \'Lumbar Region\'). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBLOC.']
  collection_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the specimen collection event. Indicates whether the collection was completed as planned, partially completed, missed, or cancelled. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scheduled|collected|missed|cancelled|partial|failed — promote to reference product if additional statuses are needed]']
  collection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The actual date and time at which the specimen was collected from the subject. This is the principal real-world event timestamp per ALCOA+ (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate) requirements. Distinct from scheduled collection time.']
  collector_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the CRC or phlebotomist who performed the specimen collection. Denormalized for audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness. Classified as confidential as it identifies site personnel.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this specimen collection record was first created in the system. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  deviation_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of any deviation from the protocol-specified collection procedure, including wrong tube type, incorrect volume, missed time window, or improper storage. Populated when has_deviation = True.']
  deviation_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the type of collection deviation observed. Used for trending and CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: timing|volume|tube_type|storage|labeling|processing|other — promote to reference product]']
  fasting_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the subject was in a fasted state at the time of specimen collection, as required by certain protocol-defined laboratory assessments (e.g., lipid panels, glucose). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBFAST.']
  has_deviation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a protocol deviation or collection irregularity was recorded for this specimen collection event. True = deviation present; False = no deviation. Triggers downstream deviation management workflow.']
  hemolysis_grade varchar [note: 'Visual or instrument-assessed grade of hemolysis (red blood cell rupture) in the collected blood specimen. Hemolysis can interfere with laboratory assay results and may require recollection.']
  is_unscheduled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this specimen collection was an unscheduled (ad hoc) event not defined in the original study protocol visit schedule. True = unscheduled; False = protocol-scheduled.']
  lipemia_grade varchar [note: 'Visual or instrument-assessed grade of lipemia (excess lipids causing turbidity) in the collected specimen. Lipemia can interfere with photometric assay results.']
  nominal_time_point varchar [note: 'Protocol-defined nominal time point label for PK/PD sample collection (e.g., \'Pre-dose\', \'0.5h\', \'1h\', \'2h\', \'4h\', \'8h\', \'24h\'). Used to align actual collection times to protocol-scheduled PK sampling windows.']
  pre_analytical_instructions varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded description of the pre-analytical processing instructions followed after collection (e.g., \'Centrifuge within 30 min at 2000 rpm\', \'Store at -80°C\', \'Protect from light\'). Documents protocol compliance for sample integrity.']
  processing_completed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which pre-analytical processing of the specimen was completed at the collection site (e.g., centrifugation, aliquoting). Used to calculate processing turnaround time and assess sample integrity.']
  recollection_reason varchar [note: 'Reason why a repeat specimen collection is required. Populated when recollection_required = True. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: insufficient_volume|hemolysis|lipemia|clotted|mislabeled|lost_in_transit|expired_kit|other — promote to reference product]']
  recollection_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a repeat specimen collection is required due to inadequate sample, collection deviation, or laboratory rejection. True = recollection needed; False = no recollection required.']
  sample_adequacy varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the collected specimen volume and quality are sufficient to perform all protocol-required laboratory analyses. Determined at the time of collection or upon receipt at the laboratory.']
  scheduled_collection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The protocol-defined date and time at which the specimen collection was planned to occur per the study visit schedule. Used to calculate collection timing deviations.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this specimen collection record originated (e.g., Medidata Rave EDC, Oracle Clinical One). Supports data lineage and integration traceability.']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the biological specimen collected (e.g., \'Whole Blood\', \'Serum\', \'Plasma\', \'Urine\', \'CSF\', \'Tissue Biopsy\', \'Saliva\'). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSPEC. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Whole Blood|Serum|Plasma|Urine|CSF|Tissue Biopsy|Saliva|Stool|Bone Marrow — promote to reference product]']
  storage_temperature_c decimal(5,1) [note: 'Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the specimen was stored at the collection site prior to shipment to the central laboratory. Deviations from protocol-specified storage conditions may compromise sample integrity.']
  time_from_dose_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'Elapsed time in hours between the subject\'s most recent investigational product dose and the specimen collection. Critical for PK (Pharmacokinetics) and DMPK (Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics) sample timing analysis.']
  tube_count varchar [note: 'The total number of tubes, vials, or containers collected during this specimen collection event. Used for chain-of-custody tracking and sample accountability.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this specimen collection record was last modified. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  volume_collected_ml decimal(10,3) [note: 'Total volume of specimen collected from the subject, expressed in millilitres (mL). Critical for PK/PD studies and for verifying adequacy of sample for planned assays.']
  volume_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the volume collected. Typically mL for blood/urine, but may be µL for microsampling or g for tissue. Ensures unambiguous interpretation of volume_collected_ml.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a scheduled or unscheduled specimen collection event at a clinical site or subject visit. Captures collection event date/time, study visit reference, protocol-scheduled vs. unscheduled flag, collector ID (CRC/phlebotomist), collection kit lot number, number of tubes/containers collected, collection deviations, and pre-analytical processing instructions followed. Links specimen collection to the study visit schedule.'
}

Lab operations/QA teams monitor SLA compliance per shipment and ap']

Business justification: Specimen shipment costs (courier, dry ice, packaging) are pass-through costs billed under the study contract. Finance teams reconcile actual shipment costs against contracted pass-through budgets and ']

  excursion_min_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Lowest temperature (in degrees Celsius) recorded by the temperature monitor/data logger during transit. Populated only when a temperature excursion is detected. Supports specimen impact assessment.']

  hazardous_material_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the shipment contains materials classified as hazardous (e.g., Category B biological substances, dry ice). True = hazardous declaration required; False = non-hazardous. Drives IATA dangerous goods documentation requirements.']
  import_permit_number varchar [note: 'Regulatory import permit or authorization number required for cross-border shipment of biological specimens in certain jurisdictions. Ensures compliance with national biosafety and import regulations.']
  lab_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the designated contact person at the receiving laboratory responsible for accepting and processing the shipment. Used for courier delivery confirmation and discrepancy resolution.']
  origin_site_number varchar [note: 'Sponsor-assigned or regulatory site number of the clinical site dispatching the specimens. Denormalized for chain-of-custody documentation and regulatory audit trail without requiring a join.']
  packaging_type varchar [note: 'Type of packaging used for the shipment, indicating the thermal protection and containment method. Relevant for regulatory compliance with IATA P650 and specimen integrity documentation.']
  protocol_visit_name varchar [note: 'Name or label of the study protocol visit (e.g., Day 1, Week 4, End of Treatment) associated with the specimen collection event. Supports SDTM domain mapping and visit-level reconciliation.']
  receipt_confirmed_by varchar [note: 'Name or user identifier of the laboratory staff member who confirmed receipt of the shipment. Part of the chain-of-custody audit trail per ALCOA+ principles.']
  received_specimen_count varchar [note: 'Actual number of specimens confirmed by the receiving laboratory upon opening the shipment. Compared against specimen_count to identify discrepancies or missing specimens.']
  rejection_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the reason the shipment was rejected at the receiving laboratory (e.g., temperature excursion, broken specimens, incorrect labeling, missing manifest). Populated only when shipment_status = rejected.']
  shipment_date timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which the shipment was handed over to the courier at the originating clinical site. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.']
  shipment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the specimen shipment. Drives chain-of-custody workflow and exception management. Values: pending (prepared, not yet dispatched), in_transit (with courier), delivered (courier confirmed delivery), received (lab confirmed receipt), rejected (refused at destination), cancelled (shipment voided).']
  shipment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the shipment by its clinical purpose. Values: routine (standard scheduled collection), urgent (expedited for safety or protocol reasons), pk_sample (Pharmacokinetics samples requiring strict timing), biomarker (exploratory biomarker specimens), backup (duplicate aliquots for archival), reshipment (replacement for a failed prior shipment).']
  specimen_count varchar [note: 'Total number of individual specimen tubes, aliquots, or containers included in this shipment as declared on the manifest. Used for reconciliation at receipt.']
  subject_count varchar [note: 'Number of distinct study subjects whose specimens are included in this shipment. Supports subject-level reconciliation and enrollment tracking at the laboratory.']
  temperature_condition varchar [note: 'Required temperature storage and transport condition for the shipment as specified in the laboratory manual. Critical for specimen integrity. Values: ambient (15–25°C), refrigerated (2–8°C), frozen (-20°C), dry_ice (-78°C), liquid_nitrogen (-196°C).']
  temperature_excursion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a temperature excursion (deviation outside the acceptable range) was detected during transit. True = excursion occurred; False = no excursion. Triggers specimen usability assessment workflow.']
  temperature_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Upper bound of the acceptable temperature range (in degrees Celsius) for this shipment as defined in the study laboratory manual. Used to evaluate temperature excursion severity.']
  temperature_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Lower bound of the acceptable temperature range (in degrees Celsius) for this shipment as defined in the study laboratory manual. Used to evaluate temperature excursion severity.']
  temperature_monitor_code varchar [note: 'Serial number or identifier of the temperature data logger or indicator device placed in the shipment. Enables retrieval of the full temperature log for excursion investigation and regulatory documentation.']
  temperature_monitor_type varchar [note: 'Type of temperature monitoring device included in the shipment. Data_logger provides continuous electronic recording; indicator_card provides a visual pass/fail indicator; none indicates no monitoring device was used.']
  tracking_number varchar [note: 'Carrier-assigned tracking number for the shipment package, enabling real-time logistics monitoring and proof-of-delivery confirmation.']
  un_number varchar [note: 'United Nations dangerous goods classification number for the shipment contents (e.g., UN3373 for Category B biological substances, UN1845 for dry ice). Required on shipping labels and documentation when hazardous_material_flag is True.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which this specimen shipment record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks lakehouse.']

  Note: 'Transactional record tracking the shipment of specimens from a clinical site to a central or reference laboratory. Captures shipment manifest ID, origin site, destination lab facility, courier name, tracking number, shipment date/time, expected arrival date, actual receipt date, temperature condition (ambient/refrigerated/frozen/dry ice), number of specimens, shipment status, and any temperature excursion flags. Supports chain of custody and specimen integrity tracking.'
}
