  edc_alert_rule_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the automated edit check or alert rule configured in Medidata Rave EDC that fires when a lab result breaches this critical value threshold. Supports automated critical value flagging at point of data entry.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date on which this critical value threshold ceases to be effective. Null indicates the threshold is currently active with no defined expiry. Supports temporal versioning and audit trail.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date from which this critical value threshold becomes effective and is applied in automated alerting workflows. Supports temporal versioning of threshold definitions.']
  escalation_pathway varchar [note: 'Defined escalation route for communicating a critical value to the appropriate clinical personnel (e.g., PI direct, CRC then PI, Medical Monitor, Sponsor Safety team, DSMB). Governs the automated notification routing logic. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pi_direct|crc_then_pi|medical_monitor|sponsor_safety|dsmb|site_medical_director|other — promote to reference product]']
  escalation_tier_2_minutes varchar [note: 'Number of minutes after initial notification attempt before escalating to the secondary contact in the escalation pathway if no acknowledgement is received.']
  fasting_state_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this critical value threshold applies only to specimens collected under fasting conditions. True = fasting required for threshold applicability; False = non-fasting or state-independent.']
  lab_facility_scope varchar [note: 'Defines the applicability of this critical value threshold to laboratory facilities: all facilities, central lab only, local lab only, or a specific named facility. Drives which lab facilities apply this threshold in automated alerting workflows.']
  loinc_code varchar [note: 'Standardized LOINC code uniquely identifying the laboratory observation or test. Enables interoperability across laboratory systems and regulatory submissions per CDISC standards.']
  notification_sla_minutes varchar [note: 'Maximum allowable time in minutes from critical value detection to confirmed clinical notification. Drives automated alerting SLA monitoring and compliance reporting. Typical values range from 15 to 60 minutes per CAP and CLIA requirements.']
  regulatory_authority_basis varchar [note: 'Regulatory authority or guideline that mandates or informs this critical value threshold definition (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA, CAP, CLIA). Supports multi-jurisdictional compliance documentation.']
  requires_repeat_confirmation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a repeat specimen analysis is required to confirm the critical value before initiating the notification workflow. True = repeat confirmation required; False = single result triggers notification.']
  sex_applicability varchar [note: 'Specifies the biological sex for which this critical value threshold applies. Some analytes (e.g., hemoglobin, creatinine) have sex-specific reference and critical ranges.']
  source_reference_document varchar [note: 'Citation or document reference (e.g., protocol section, lab manual version, CAP guideline) from which this critical value threshold was derived. Supports traceability and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological specimen from which the analyte is measured (e.g., blood, urine, plasma, serum). Critical value thresholds may differ by specimen type. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: blood|urine|plasma|serum|csf|tissue|saliva|other — promote to reference product]']
  test_system_code varchar [note: 'Internal or sponsor-defined code for the specific laboratory test or panel within the clinical trial management system (e.g., Medidata Rave EDC lab test code). Used for system-to-system mapping.']
  threshold_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the critical value threshold record. Active = in use for alerting; Inactive = retired; Superseded = replaced by a newer version; Under Review = pending clinical or regulatory review.']
  threshold_type varchar [note: 'Defines whether the critical value threshold is an absolute numeric value, a delta change from baseline, or a percent change from a prior result. Determines the comparison logic applied during automated alerting.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Standard unit of measurement for the critical value thresholds (e.g., mmol/L, g/dL, 10^9/L, mg/dL). Must align with the unit used in the corresponding lab result to enable automated threshold comparison.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this critical value threshold record. Required for ALCOA+ data integrity and 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier for this critical value threshold record (e.g., 1.0, 2.1). Incremented when threshold values, SLA, or escalation pathway are modified. Supports ALCOA+ data integrity requirements.']

  Note: 'Reference master defining critical (panic) value thresholds for laboratory analytes that require immediate clinical notification. Captures analyte, LOINC code, critical low threshold, critical high threshold, unit, notification SLA (minutes), escalation pathway, and lab facility applicability. Drives automated critical value alerting workflows and safety reporting integration with Oracle Argus Safety.'
}

  uloq decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper Limit of Quantification — the highest analyte concentration that can be reliably quantified within the validated dynamic range. Samples above ULOQ must be diluted and re-assayed. Expressed in the unit defined by lloq_uloq_unit.']

  validation_date date [note: 'Date on which the bioanalytical method validation was formally completed and the validation report was approved. Marks the point from which the assay is considered fit for regulated use in clinical sample analysis.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Current regulatory validation tier of the assay. \'Validated\' indicates full GLP/GCP-compliant validation per FDA/EMA/ICH M10 guidelines; \'Qualified\' indicates fit-for-purpose qualification; \'Exploratory\' indicates early-phase research use only; \'In Validation\' indicates validation in progress; \'Retired\' indicates the assay is no longer in use.   version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the assay method (e.g., \'v1.0\', \'v2.1\'). Incremented when the assay undergoes method changes requiring partial or full re-validation. Enables traceability of which assay version was used for each study\'s sample analysis.']
  weighting_factor varchar [note: 'Statistical weighting factor applied to the calibration curve regression to minimize heteroscedasticity (e.g., \'1/x\', \'1/x²\', \'none\'). Documented in the validation report and applied consistently during sample analysis.']

  Note: 'Master definition of a validated bioanalytical assay used to quantify drug concentrations, biomarkers, or immunogenicity in clinical trial samples. Supports DMPK and PK/PD data generation.'
}

Table laboratory.lab_qualification {
  lab_qualification_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the lab_qualification association']
  clinical_program_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the clinical development program for which this laboratory facility is qualified.']
  lab_facility_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the laboratory facility being qualified for this clinical program.']
  contract_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier for the vendor contract or master service agreement governing the laboratory facility\'s engagement for this clinical program. Links to the procurement or legal contract management system.']
  primary_lab_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this laboratory facility is designated as the primary (central) laboratory for this clinical program. A program may have one primary lab and multiple specialty or backup labs.']
  qualification_date date [note: 'Date on which the laboratory facility was formally qualified to perform specimen analysis for this clinical program. Marks the start of the approved engagement for regulatory audit trail purposes.']
  qualification_status varchar [note: 'Current sponsor or CRO qualification status of the laboratory facility for this specific clinical program. Reflects the outcome of the qualification assessment and drives whether the lab may receive specimens for this program.']
  scope_of_services varchar [note: 'Narrative or structured description of the specific assay panels, specimen types, and analytical services this laboratory facility is approved to perform for this clinical program (e.g., hematology, PK assays, biomarker panels).']
  sponsor_approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor formally approved this laboratory facility for use in this clinical program. May differ from qualification_date when sponsor review follows CRO qualification.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal qualification and engagement contract between a lab_facility and a clinical_program. It captures the sponsor-approved, program-specific qualification of a laboratory facility to perform defined specimen analyses for a clinical development program. Each record links one lab_facility to one clinical_program and carries attributes — qualification status, approval dates, scope of services, and contract reference — that exist only in the context of this program-facility relationship and cannot reside on either master entity alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials operations, a clinical program selects and qualifies multiple laboratory facilities (central lab, PK lab, biomarker lab, etc.) to support its studies, and each lab facility simultaneously serves multiple clinical programs across different sponsors and therapeutic areas. This is an actively managed vendor oversight relationship — sponsors and CROs formally qualify labs per program, track approval status, define scope of services, and maintain contract references for each program-facility pairing. The relationship is a recognized operational business concept in clinical procurement and vendor management.'
}

Table laboratory.panel_composition {
  panel_composition_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the panel_composition association']
  lab_analyte_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the constituent analyte included in this panel composition']
  lab_panel_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the parent lab panel whose composition this record defines']
  analyte_count varchar [note: 'Total number of individual analytes (tests) included in this panel. Provides a quick reference for panel complexity and is used in turnaround time estimation and cost modelling. [Moved from lab_panel: This INT on lab_panel is a derived/calculated value that counts the number of analytes in the panel. Once panel_composition is the authoritative source of panel membership, analyte_count becomes a computed aggregate (COUNT of panel_composition records for a given lab_panel_id) and should not be stored as a static attribute on lab_panel, where it would require manual maintenance and is prone to drift.]']
  analyte_list varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of analyte names or LBTESTCD codes included in this panel (e.g., \'ALT, AST, ALP, TBILI, DBILI, GGT\'). Provides a human-readable summary of panel content for protocol review and eCRF design. [Moved from lab_panel: This denormalized comma-separated STRING on lab_panel is an anti-pattern that attempts to capture the M:N panel composition relationship in a single column. It cannot support referential integrity, per-analyte metadata, or efficient querying. The panel_composition association table fully replaces this attribute, and analyte_list should be removed from lab_panel.]']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'The date on which this analyte was removed from this panel\'s composition. A null value indicates the analyte is currently active in the panel. Used to reconstruct historical panel composition at any point in time for audit and regulatory purposes.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'The date from which this analyte was included in this panel\'s composition. Supports version-controlled panel composition tracking across protocol amendments. A null value indicates the analyte has been part of the panel since the panel\'s inception.']
  is_required_analyte boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this analyte is mandatory for the panel to be considered complete and reportable. When false, the analyte is optional or conditionally performed. Belongs to the composition relationship as the same analyte may be required in one panel but optional in another.']
  minimum_volume_contribution_ml decimal [note: 'The minimum specimen volume in millilitres required specifically for this analyte\'s performance within this panel. Used to calculate total panel specimen volume requirements. Belongs to the composition relationship as volume requirements may differ per panel context.']
  reporting_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this analyte\'s result is included in the panel\'s standard report output. Some analytes may be performed internally for QC or calculation purposes but not reported to the sponsor or investigator site.']
  sequence_order varchar [note: 'The ordered display/reporting position of this analyte within the panel. Determines the sequence in which analyte results appear on lab reports and eCRF panels. Belongs to the composition relationship, not to the analyte or panel alone.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal composition contract between a lab_panel and its constituent lab_analytes. It captures the version-controlled membership of each analyte within a panel as actively managed by lab directors and protocol teams. Each record links one lab_panel to one lab_analyte and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this panel-analyte relationship: the analyte\'s position in the panel, its required/optional status, its specimen volume contribution, its reporting inclusion, and the effective date range of its membership. This is the authoritative source for panel composition used in LIMS configuration, SDTM LB domain mapping, and protocol amendment tracking.. Existence Justification: In clinical laboratory operations, a test panel is formally defined as a named collection of specific analytes — a CBC panel contains hemoglobin, hematocrit, WBC, platelets, etc., while a CMP panel contains glucose, BUN, creatinine, electrolytes, etc. This composition is actively managed by lab directors and protocol teams, is version-controlled per protocol amendment, and is a recognized concept in LIMS systems and CDISC SDTM LB domain modeling. One panel contains many analytes, and one analyte (e.g., Sodium) appears in many panels (CMP, BMP, Electrolyte Panel) — this is a genuine operational M:N with full reciprocity. The relationship carries its own data: sequence order within the panel, whether the analyte is required vs. optional, minimum volume contribution, reporting flags, and effective dates for version control.'
}

Table laboratory.sow_lab_panel_requirement {
  sow_lab_panel_requirement_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the sow_lab_panel_requirement association']
  lab_panel_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the laboratory test panel catalog entry that is contractually included in this SOW']
  scope_of_work_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Scope of Work document under which this lab panel is contracted']
  central_lab_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SOW mandates that this panel be performed at a central laboratory. Overrides or confirms the lab_type attribute on the panel catalog for the purposes of this specific contractual engagement.']
  contracted_turnaround_days decimal [note: 'Negotiated turnaround time in days from specimen receipt to result delivery, as agreed in this specific SOW. May differ from the catalog turnaround_time_hours on lab_panel, which represents a general SLA target.']
  panel_requirement_type varchar [note: 'Classification of why this lab panel is included in the SOW — e.g., safety monitoring, pharmacokinetics, biomarker assessment. The same panel may serve different purposes in different SOWs.']
  specimen_volume_contracted_ml decimal [note: 'Contracted specimen volume in millilitres agreed for this panel under this SOW. May differ from the catalog minimum (specimen_volume_ml on lab_panel) due to sponsor-specific protocol requirements or pooling arrangements.']
  unit_price decimal [note: 'Per-panel unit price negotiated between the sponsor and CRO under this SOW. Pricing is specific to the SOW-panel combination and is not a property of the panel catalog or the SOW header.']
  visit_applicability varchar [note: 'Specification of which study visit timepoints (e.g., Screening, Day 1, Week 4, End of Treatment) require this panel under this SOW. Encoded as a pipe-separated list of visit codes or a free-text schedule description.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between scope_of_work and lab_panel in clinical research operations. It captures the formal contractual inclusion of a specific laboratory test panel within a Scope of Work, recording the negotiated terms (unit price, turnaround commitment, visit applicability) that govern how the CRO will deliver that panel for the study. Each record links one scope_of_work to one lab_panel with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual relationship — they are neither properties of the panel catalog nor of the SOW document alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical research operations, a Scope of Work (SOW) contractually specifies which laboratory panels the CRO will perform for a given study, and a single lab panel (e.g., a CBC safety panel or PK panel) can appear across many different SOWs for different studies or sponsors. The business actively manages this relationship as a \'contracted lab panel requirement\' — negotiating unit pricing, turnaround commitments, and visit applicability per panel per SOW. This is not derivable from transactional data; it is a contractual record created during SOW authoring and updated during amendments.'
}

Table laboratory.lab_service_contract {
  lab_service_contract_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the lab_service_contract association']
  lab_facility_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the laboratory facility engaged under this service contract.']
  study_budget_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the study budget under which this lab facility is contracted.']
  amendment_number varchar [note: 'Sequential integer tracking the number of amendments applied to this lab service contract record. Incremented each time contracted_rate, service_scope, or terms are formally revised. Supports audit trail for SOX-compliant budget change management.']
  contract_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this lab service contract record. Drives workflow approvals and determines whether the facility is authorized to invoice against this study budget.']
  contracted_rate decimal [note: 'The negotiated unit rate agreed with the lab facility for specimen processing services under this specific study budget. Varies per facility-study combination and cannot reside on either the facility master or the budget master alone.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the contracted_rate. May differ from the study budget\'s base currency when the lab facility is in a different country.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which the contracted terms between this lab facility and this study budget become financially binding. Used for cost accrual timing and sponsor invoicing alignment.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which the contracted terms expire or are superseded by an amendment. Supports contract lifecycle management and budget re-forecasting.']
  service_scope varchar [note: 'Narrative or structured description of the assay panels, specimen types, and analytical services covered under this facility-budget contract. Defines what the lab is authorized and budgeted to perform for this study.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between lab_facility and study_budget. It captures the facility-specific financial and operational terms under which a laboratory facility is engaged to perform specimen analysis services for a specific study budget. Each record links one lab_facility to one study_budget with attributes — contracted rate, service scope, effective dates, and amendment tracking — that exist only in the context of this study-facility contractual relationship. Serves as the operational record for lab vendor cost management, sponsor invoicing reconciliation, and budget variance analysis at the facility level.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials operations, a lab facility (e.g., a central lab or bioanalytical lab) is contracted to serve multiple studies — each with its own budget, contracted rates, service scope, and amendment history. Conversely, a single study budget allocates funds across multiple lab facilities (central lab, local labs, PK lab), each under distinct contractual terms. This relationship is actively managed by finance and lab operations teams as a \'Lab Service Contract\' or \'Lab Budget Allocation\', carrying facility-specific contracted rates, service scope, effective dates, and amendment numbers that belong to neither the facility master record nor the budget master record alone.'
}

  effective_from_date date [note: 'The date from which this kit definition version becomes effective and may be used for manufacturing and dispensing. Supports protocol amendment versioning of kit configurations.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'The date after which this kit definition version is no longer valid for new manufacturing or dispensing. Null indicates the definition is currently active with no planned end date.']
  is_blinded boolean [note: 'Indicates whether kits of this definition are blinded (True) or open-label (False). A key flag for RTSM dispensing logic and unblinding procedures.']
  is_comparator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this kit definition contains a comparator drug (True) rather than the investigational product or placebo. Used for supply chain sourcing differentiation and regulatory reporting.']
  is_rescue_medication boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this kit definition represents a rescue medication (True) rather than the primary study treatment. Rescue medication kits follow different dispensing and accountability rules.']
  kit_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the kit definition including its intended use, contents summary, and any special handling instructions relevant to the kit template.']
  kit_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name for the kit definition as configured in the RTSM system (e.g., \'Study XYZ Arm A 10mg Tablet 28-Day Supply\'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for this MASTER_RESOURCE.']
  kit_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to this kit definition template in the RTSM system. Used by manufacturers, depots, and sites to reference the kit configuration. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this MASTER_RESOURCE.']
  kit_number_range_end varchar [note: 'The last sequential kit number in the numeric range allocated to physical kits manufactured from this kit definition. Together with kit_number_range_start, defines the total pool of physical kits that can be generated from this definition.']
  kit_number_range_start varchar [note: 'The first sequential kit number in the numeric range allocated to physical kits manufactured from this kit definition. Used by RTSM to assign unique kit numbers to physical instances during manufacturing.']
  kit_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the kit definition template. Draft indicates under development; approved indicates validated and ready for manufacture; active indicates in use for dispensing; superseded indicates replaced by a newer version; retired indicates no longer in use. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this MASTER_RESOURCE.']
  kit_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the kit by its therapeutic content category. Distinguishes between active drug kits, placebo kits, comparator kits, combination kits, device kits, and ancillary supply kits. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE for this MASTER_RESOURCE.']
  label_language_code varchar [note: 'ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) for the primary language of the kit label text (e.g., \'en\', \'fr\', \'de\', \'ja\'). Required for multi-country studies with country-specific labeling.']
  label_text varchar [note: 'The regulatory-approved label text to be printed on physical kits manufactured from this definition. Must comply with applicable labeling regulations and may include study number, kit number, storage conditions, and investigational use statement.']
  manufacturing_site_code varchar [note: 'The code identifying the manufacturing or packaging site responsible for producing physical kits from this definition. Used for supply chain traceability and GMP compliance.']
  max_storage_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for kits of this definition. Used for cold-chain monitoring alerts and excursion detection.']
  min_storage_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for kits of this definition. Used for cold-chain monitoring alerts and excursion detection.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this kit definition record was last modified. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and change tracking for regulatory inspection readiness.']
  pack_size varchar [note: 'The number of individual dosage units (e.g., tablets, capsules, vials) contained in one physical kit of this definition. Used for supply planning, dispensing calculations, and accountability reconciliation.']
  pack_size_unit varchar [note: 'The unit descriptor for the pack size count (e.g., tablet, capsule, vial). Clarifies what each unit in the pack_size count represents. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|vial|ampoule|syringe|patch|sachet|bottle — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  randomization_scheme varchar [note: 'The randomization methodology applied to kits of this definition type within the RTSM. Determines how kits are allocated to subjects during enrollment and randomization events.']
  retest_period_days varchar [note: 'Number of days from manufacture after which kits of this definition must be retested before continued use. Applicable for IMP components with defined retest periods rather than fixed expiry dates.']
  return_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether used or unused kits of this definition must be returned to the depot or sponsor for accountability reconciliation and destruction. Drives returns logistics workflows.']
  rtsm_kit_type_code varchar [note: 'The internal kit type code as configured in the Medidata Rave RTSM system. Used for system-to-system integration and reconciliation between the RTSM and downstream data systems.']
  shelf_life_days varchar [note: 'The approved shelf life duration in days for kits manufactured from this definition, measured from the date of manufacture. Used to calculate expiry dates on physical kit instances and to trigger re-supply or destruction workflows.']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'Required storage condition for kits of this definition type. Drives cold-chain logistics planning, depot storage allocation, and site storage compliance monitoring.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version number of this kit definition (e.g., \'1.0\', \'2.1\'). Incremented when the kit definition is amended due to protocol changes, labeling updates, or manufacturing changes. Supports audit trail and regulatory traceability.']
  visit_type varchar [note: 'The type of study visit at which this kit definition is intended to be dispensed (e.g., baseline, treatment, follow-up, unscheduled). Drives RTSM dispensing schedule configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screening|baseline|treatment|follow_up|unscheduled|end_of_study|early_termination — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Defines randomization kit configurations used in RTSM (Medidata Rave). Captures kit type, treatment arm association, blinding level, component IMPs, pack size, label text, kit number range, and applicable study/protocol version. Serves as the template from which physical kits are manufactured and assigned. Distinct from kit_inventory which tracks physical instances.'
}

  qty_destroyed varchar [note: 'Cumulative number of IMP units or kits that have been destroyed at or from this location, including expired, damaged, or returned-and-destroyed stock. Required for regulatory accountability reconciliation.']
  qty_dispensed varchar [note: 'Cumulative number of IMP units or kits dispensed to study subjects at this location since the study began or since the last accountability reconciliation period. Sourced from dispensing records in the RTSM.']
  qty_expired varchar [note: 'Number of IMP units or kits that have passed their expiry date at this location and are no longer eligible for dispensing. Tracked separately for regulatory accountability and waste reporting.']
  qty_on_hand varchar [note: 'Current physical count of IMP units or kits available at this location, excluding quarantined, allocated, and reserved stock. Represents the net usable inventory at the time of the last update. Used as the primary metric for resupply trigger evaluation.']
  qty_quarantined varchar [note: 'Number of IMP units or kits currently placed in quarantine at this location due to quality concerns, temperature excursions, damaged packaging, or pending investigation. These units are not available for dispensing.']
  qty_received varchar [note: 'Cumulative number of IMP units or kits received at this location since the study began or since the last accountability reconciliation period. Sourced from inbound shipment confirmations in the RTSM.']
  qty_returned varchar [note: 'Cumulative number of IMP units or kits returned from subjects or from this site to the depot or sponsor for destruction or reconciliation. Used in accountability reconciliation calculations.']
  reconciliation_date date [note: 'Date on which the most recent IMP accountability reconciliation was completed and approved for this inventory position. Required for regulatory inspection readiness and study close-out documentation.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this inventory record was first created in the system, conforming to ALCOA+ principles of contemporaneous data capture. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this inventory record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements under ALCOA+ and 21 CFR Part 11, and enables change detection in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.']
  reorder_point varchar [note: 'Minimum quantity threshold at which a resupply request should be triggered for this IMP or kit type at this location. When qty_on_hand falls at or below this value, the RTSM or supply planner initiates a replenishment shipment.']
  reorder_qty varchar [note: 'Standard replenishment quantity to be shipped when a resupply is triggered for this location and IMP/kit type. Defined in the supply plan and used by the RTSM to generate resupply orders automatically.']
  resupply_request_date date [note: 'Date on which the most recent resupply request was initiated for this inventory position. Used to track supply chain responsiveness and expected delivery timelines.']
  resupply_triggered boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an active resupply request has been triggered for this inventory position. Set to True when qty_on_hand falls at or below the reorder_point and a resupply order has been initiated in the RTSM or supply management system.']
  retest_date date [note: 'Date by which the IMP batch must be retested to confirm continued stability and suitability for use. Applicable for products with defined retest periods rather than fixed expiry dates. Triggers stability testing workflows.']
  rtsm_location_code varchar [note: 'The location identifier assigned to this site or depot within the RTSM system (Medidata Rave). Used to reconcile inventory records between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational RTSM source system.']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'Required storage condition for the IMP or kit at this location, as specified in the Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier (IMPD) or protocol. Drives cold-chain logistics planning and compliance monitoring. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: room_temperature|refrigerated|frozen|ultra_frozen|controlled_room_temperature|light_protected — promote to reference product if additional conditions are needed]']
  storage_condition_compliant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the current storage conditions at this location are compliant with the required storage condition specification for this IMP or kit type. Set to False when a temperature excursion or storage deviation is recorded, triggering quarantine and quality review.']
  temperature_excursion_count varchar [note: 'Cumulative number of recorded temperature excursion events for this inventory position at this location. Used to assess cold-chain compliance history and inform quarantine or destruction decisions.']
  treatment_arm_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the treatment arm or randomization group associated with this kit type inventory (e.g., active drug, placebo, dose level A). For blinded studies, this field may be restricted to unblinded personnel only.']

  Note: 'Tracks IMP and kit stock positions at supply chain nodes (investigational sites and depots). Each record represents current inventory levels by IMP/kit type at a specific location, including quantity on-hand, received, dispensed, allocated, quarantined, returned, and expired. Records storage condition compliance, last physical count date, and location type (site or depot). Enables accountability reconciliation, resupply trigger management, and regulatory inventory reporting. Linked to site or depot via location reference.'
}

  destination_node_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the supply chain destination node (e.g., site name, depot name). Supports logistics documentation and regulatory accountability records.']
  destination_node_type varchar [note: 'Type of supply chain node to which the shipment is directed (e.g., clinical site, central depot, manufacturer). Supports supply chain network mapping and inventory accountability.']
  destruction_certificate_number varchar [note: 'Certificate number issued upon confirmed destruction of returned or expired IMP. Required for regulatory accountability reconciliation and GMP compliance documentation.']

  dispatch_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time the IMP shipment was dispatched from the origin node. Supports cold-chain elapsed time calculations and ALCOA+ data integrity requirements.']
  excursion_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Total cumulative duration in minutes during which the shipment temperature was outside the specified storage condition range. Used for product impact assessment and quality disposition decisions.']

  min_recorded_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum temperature in degrees Celsius recorded by the cold-chain data logger during transit. Used to assess whether the IMP was exposed to freezing or sub-optimal low temperatures.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional operational notes, special handling instructions, or comments related to the shipment (e.g., fragile contents, priority handling, deviation observations).']

  origin_node_type varchar [note: 'Type of supply chain node from which the shipment originates (e.g., manufacturer, central depot, clinical site, CRO warehouse). Used for supply chain network mapping and accountability.']
  quarantine_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the shipment or its contents have been placed under quarantine pending quality investigation (e.g., following a temperature excursion or damaged packaging). Prevents dispensing of affected kits to subjects.']
  rtsm_shipment_ref varchar [note: 'Source system shipment reference identifier from the RTSM module (Medidata Rave). Used for cross-system reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational RTSM system.']
  shipment_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable shipment reference number generated by the RTSM (Medidata Rave) or logistics provider. Used for cross-system reconciliation, carrier communication, and regulatory accountability documentation.']
  shipment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the IMP shipment within the clinical supply chain workflow. Drives accountability reconciliation and RTSM inventory updates. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned|dispatched|in_transit|delivered|returned|destroyed|cancelled — promote to reference product]']
  shipment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the shipment purpose within the clinical supply chain. Distinguishes initial site supply, resupply, site-to-site transfer, returns to depot, and emergency shipments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: initial_supply|resupply|return|destruction|transfer|emergency — promote to reference product]']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'Required storage temperature condition for the IMP during transit and at the destination (e.g., refrigerated 2-8°C, frozen -20°C, ambient 15-25°C). Drives cold-chain logistics requirements and excursion assessment.']
  temperature_excursion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a temperature excursion (deviation from required storage condition) was detected during transit. Triggers quality investigation, product impact assessment, and potential quarantine of affected kits.']
  tracking_number varchar [note: 'Carrier-assigned tracking number for the shipment. Used to monitor real-time transit status, confirm delivery, and investigate temperature excursions or delays.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the shipment record. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements, change tracking, and data integrity compliance per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  waybill_number varchar [note: 'Air waybill (AWB) or bill of lading number issued by the carrier for the shipment. Used for customs documentation, carrier liability, and logistics traceability.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of IMP/kit shipments between supply chain nodes (manufacturer to depot, depot to site, site to site, site to depot for returns). Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM and logistics provider integrations.'

  temperature_excursion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a cold-chain temperature excursion was recorded or reported for the returned IMP during storage or transit (True = excursion occurred). Triggers quality investigation and potential destruction.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp recording the most recent modification to this return record. Required for audit trail integrity and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  verification_date date [note: 'Date on which the CRA or pharmacist completed Source Data Verification (SDV) of the return record against source documents at the site or depot.']
  verified_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) or pharmacist who verified the return quantities and condition during a monitoring visit or depot check. Supports Source Data Verification (SDV).']

Captures return type (subject return, site-to-depot, expired stock), kit numbers or quantities returned, return date, condition on return (intact, partially used, damaged), reconciliation status, and destruction authorization reference. Essential for drug accountability reconciliation and regulatory compliance.'

  excursion_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone) at which the temperature excursion began — i.e., when the temperature first breached the defined threshold. This is the principal real-world event time for the excursion. Critical for duration calculation and impact assessment.']
  excursion_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the excursion event record. Drives QA workflow: open (newly detected), under_investigation (impact assessment in progress), pending_disposition (awaiting sponsor/QA decision), closed (disposition finalized), voided (false alarm or data entry error confirmed).']
  excursion_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the excursion by the nature of the breach: high_temperature (exceeded upper limit), low_temperature (fell below lower limit), freeze_thaw (frozen product that should not be), humidity (relative humidity breach), combined (multiple parameter breach simultaneously).']
  impact_assessment_outcome varchar [note: 'The outcome of the scientific/QA impact assessment determining the usability of the affected IMP: use (product confirmed acceptable for continued use), quarantine (product held pending further evaluation), destroy (product deemed unusable and scheduled for destruction), pending (assessment not yet completed), return_to_sponsor (product to be returned to sponsor for evaluation). Critical for GCP compliance and patient safety.']
  location_type varchar [note: 'Categorizes where in the cold-chain the excursion occurred: depot (central or regional IMP warehouse), site (investigational site pharmacy or storage), in_transit (during shipment between locations), courier_hub (third-party logistics hub), customs (held at customs/border control).']
  logger_calibration_date date [note: 'The most recent calibration date of the temperature data logger at the time of the excursion. Required to validate the reliability of the recorded temperature data for GCP audit readiness and regulatory submissions.']
  lower_threshold_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'The minimum acceptable storage temperature (in degrees Celsius) defined for the affected IMP, as specified in the kit definition or product stability data. Breach of this threshold constitutes a low-temperature excursion.']
  max_temp_recorded_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'The highest temperature value (in degrees Celsius) recorded during the excursion event. Used to assess the severity of a high-temperature excursion against product stability specifications.']
  mean_kinetic_temp_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'The Mean Kinetic Temperature (MKT) in degrees Celsius calculated for the excursion period. MKT is the single calculated temperature that, if maintained over the storage period, would produce the same thermal stress as the actual temperature fluctuations. Used per USP <1079> and WHO guidelines for stability impact assessment.']
  min_temp_recorded_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'The lowest temperature value (in degrees Celsius) recorded during the excursion event. Used to assess the severity of a low-temperature or freeze-thaw excursion against product stability specifications.']
  replacement_kits_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether replacement IMP kits need to be dispatched to the affected site or depot as a result of the disposition decision (e.g., quarantine or destroy outcome). Drives supply replenishment workflow in the RTSM (Medidata Rave).']
  reported_by varchar [note: 'Name or user identifier of the person (e.g., CRC, CRA, site pharmacist, depot manager) who first reported or logged the temperature excursion into the system. Supports ALCOA+ attributability requirements.']
  reported_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the excursion was formally reported or entered into the system. May differ from excursion_start_timestamp if there was a delay in detection or reporting. Supports ALCOA+ contemporaneity assessment.']
  root_cause_category varchar [note: 'High-level categorization of the root cause identified during the CAPA or investigation process: equipment_failure (refrigeration/monitoring device malfunction), process_failure (SOP not followed), human_error (incorrect handling), logistics_failure (carrier/transit failure), environmental (external weather or facility event), unknown (root cause not yet determined). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|process_failure|human_error|logistics_failure|environmental|unknown — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]']
  root_cause_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the identified root cause of the temperature excursion, as documented during the QA investigation. Supports CAPA development and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  rtsm_excursion_reference varchar [note: 'The excursion or alert reference identifier as recorded in the RTSM system (Medidata Rave IRT/RTSM module). Used for cross-system traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational source system.']
  sponsor_notification_date date [note: 'The date on which the sponsor was formally notified of the temperature excursion. Null if sponsor_notification_required is False or notification has not yet been sent. Used to track compliance with contractual and regulatory notification timelines.']
  sponsor_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the sponsor must be formally notified of this excursion per the clinical supply agreement or protocol requirements. True = notification required; False = not required (e.g., minor excursion within pre-defined acceptable limits).']
  stability_data_reviewed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the product stability data (from the Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier or stability package) was formally reviewed as part of the impact assessment for this excursion. True = reviewed; False = not yet reviewed. Required for GCP compliance documentation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this temperature excursion record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and incremental data processing in the Databricks Lakehouse silver layer.']
  upper_threshold_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'The maximum acceptable storage temperature (in degrees Celsius) defined for the affected IMP, as specified in the kit definition or product stability data. Breach of this threshold constitutes a high-temperature excursion.']

  Note: 'Records cold-chain temperature excursion events detected during IMP storage or transit. Captures excursion start and end timestamps, affected location (depot, site, in-transit), temperature range breached, duration, affected kit/batch numbers, impact assessment outcome (use/quarantine/destroy), and sponsor/QA disposition decision. Critical for cold-chain compliance and GCP audit readiness.'

  rejection_reason varchar [note: 'Reason provided by the regulatory authority for rejecting the import permit application. Populated when permit_status is \'rejected\'. Used to guide resubmission and CAPA activities.']
  renewal_lead_time_days varchar [note: 'Number of calendar days before permit expiry that the renewal application must be submitted to the issuing authority. Used to trigger automated renewal reminders and prevent supply disruption.']
  renewal_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this import permit requires periodic renewal before the study completes. Triggers proactive renewal workflow to prevent supply chain disruption due to permit expiry.']
  requires_cold_chain boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the IMP requires cold-chain logistics management during import (refrigerated, frozen, or ultra-frozen transport). Drives logistics planning and customs clearance prioritization.']
  revocation_date date [note: 'Date on which the regulatory authority revoked a previously approved import permit. Populated only when permit_status is \'revoked\'. Triggers immediate shipment hold and regulatory notification.']
  revocation_reason varchar [note: 'Reason provided by the regulatory authority for revoking a previously approved import permit. Populated when permit_status is \'revoked\'. Triggers regulatory notification and supply chain hold.']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'Required storage condition for the IMP as specified on the import permit and in the IMP dossier. Drives cold-chain logistics requirements during import and customs clearance. Must align with kit_definition storage conditions.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the import permit record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  utilized_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Cumulative quantity of IMP actually imported against this permit to date. Used to track permit utilization, remaining authorized quantity, and accountability reconciliation. Expressed in the same unit as permitted_quantity_unit.']
  utilized_shipment_count varchar [note: 'Number of shipments that have been made against this permit to date. Used to track permit utilization and determine remaining shipment capacity for multi_shipment permits.']
  valid_from_date date [note: 'Date from which the import permit is legally effective and shipments may be made under its authority. Typically coincides with or follows the approval date.']
  valid_to_date date [note: 'Date on which the import permit expires and is no longer valid for authorizing IMP shipments. Critical for preventing shipment delays due to expired permits. Null for open-ended permits.']

  Note: 'Manages country-level import permits and licenses required for cross-border IMP shipments. Captures permit number, issuing authority, country, IMP reference, permitted quantity, permit validity dates, application date, approval date, and permit status. Enables regulatory compliance tracking for international clinical supply logistics and prevents shipment delays due to missing permits.'
}

  qty_on_hand varchar [note: 'Total number of kits or units of this IMP batch currently physically present at the depot, regardless of allocation status. The gross stock figure before netting allocated, quarantined, or expired quantities.']
  qty_quarantined varchar [note: 'Number of kits or units placed under quarantine status due to quality investigations, temperature excursions, damaged packaging, or pending QP release. Quarantined stock is excluded from available supply.']
  qty_returned varchar [note: 'Number of kits or units returned from clinical sites to this depot. Returned stock is typically quarantined pending QP review before any disposition decision (reuse, destruction, or reconciliation).']
  quarantine_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code explaining why stock was placed in quarantine status. Required for GMP deviation documentation and QP disposition decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Temperature_Excursion|Damaged_Packaging|QP_Hold|Recall|Stability_Failure|Pending_Release|Investigation — promote to reference product]']
  receipt_date date [note: 'Date on which this batch/kit stock was physically received at the depot. Used for FIFO/FEFO inventory management, shelf-life calculations, and GMP receipt documentation.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this depot inventory record was first created in the system, typically upon receipt of the batch at the depot. Supports audit trail and ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation requirements.']
  reorder_quantity varchar [note: 'Standard quantity to be ordered when stock falls below the minimum threshold. Used by RTSM and supply planners to generate replenishment requests to the manufacturing site or central depot.']
  retest_date date [note: 'Date by which the IMP batch must be retested to confirm continued potency and stability before further use. Applicable for products with retest periods rather than hard expiry dates.']
  rtsm_inventory_code varchar [note: 'Identifier assigned to this inventory record within the RTSM system (Medidata Rave). Enables bidirectional reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational RTSM source system.']
  storage_condition_zone varchar [note: 'Temperature-controlled storage zone within the depot where this inventory is held (e.g., Ambient, Refrigerated 2–8°C, Frozen -20°C, Ultra-Low -80°C). Drives cold-chain logistics and compliance with IMP storage requirements.']
  temperature_excursion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a temperature excursion event has been recorded for this inventory batch during storage at the depot. A True value triggers quarantine and QP review before further use.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'The dispensing or counting unit used for all quantity fields in this inventory record (e.g., Kit, Vial, Tablet). Ensures consistent quantity interpretation across RTSM, ERP, and accountability reports. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Kit|Vial|Tablet|Capsule|Syringe|Bottle|Blister_Pack — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Tracks IMP and kit stock levels held at each depot, including quantities by batch, kit type, and storage condition zone. Records receipt date, current quantity on-hand, quantity allocated for pending shipments, quantity quarantined, quantity expired, and last physical inventory count. Distinct from site_inventory which tracks site-level stock; depot_inventory covers central and regional warehouse holdings.'
}

Table supply.budget_allocation {
  budget_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the supply_budget_allocation association']
  budget_line_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the budget line item covered by this supply allocation']
  supply_plan_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the supply plan that drives this budget allocation']
  allocation_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this supply budget allocation record. Tracks whether the allocation is in draft, actively in use, superseded by a newer supply plan version, or closed. Required to manage versioned supply plan amendments.']
  cost_category varchar [note: 'The supply cost category (e.g., manufacturing, packaging, cold-chain distribution, destruction) that this allocation covers. Classifies which aspect of the supply plan is being mapped to this budget line.']
  period_end_date date [note: 'End date of the time period during which this supply plan-to-budget line allocation is active and applicable. Together with period_start_date, bounds the financial planning window for this allocation.']
  period_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the time period during which this supply plan-to-budget line allocation is active and applicable. Defines the temporal scope of this specific allocation record.']
  planned_quantity decimal [note: 'Quantity of IMP units or supply activities allocated from this supply plan to this specific budget line. Belongs to the allocation, not to either the supply plan or budget line alone, as the same supply plan may allocate different quantities to different cost categories.']
  unit_cost decimal [note: 'Cost per unit applied to this specific supply plan-to-budget line allocation. May differ from the budget line\'s standard unit cost when supply plan amendments introduce revised cost assumptions for a specific allocation.']
  variance_amount decimal [note: 'Tracked variance between the planned supply cost and the actual or revised cost for this specific supply plan-to-budget line pairing. Enables clinical supply finance teams to perform variance analysis at the allocation level.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between supply_plan and budget_line. It captures the operational mapping maintained by clinical supply finance teams that links specific supply plan versions to granular budget line items, tracking the quantity, unit cost, cost category, time period, and variance for each allocation. Each record links one supply_plan to one budget_line with attributes that exist only in the context of this financial-operational reconciliation relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical trial operations, a supply plan covers multiple cost categories (manufacturing, packaging, distribution, destruction) each represented as distinct budget lines, while a single budget line (e.g., IMP manufacturing) is informed by and allocated across multiple supply plan versions as the study evolves through amendments and planning cycles. Clinical supply finance teams actively maintain and manage this supply plan-to-budget line mapping as a recognized operational artifact, tracking quantity allocations, unit costs, and variances per pairing. This is not an analytical derivation — it is an actively managed financial-operational reconciliation record that bridges supply planning and study budgeting.'
}

Table supply.contracted_supply_item {
  contracted_supply_item_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the contracted_supply_item association']
  imp_master_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the investigational medicinal product master record that is included in this contracted supply scope.']
  study_contract_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Clinical Trial Agreement under which this IMP supply scope is contracted.']
  contracted_quantity decimal [note: 'The total quantity of this IMP agreed to be supplied under this specific contract, expressed in the IMP\'s dispensing unit. Belongs to the relationship because the same IMP may have different contracted quantities across different study contracts.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this IMP\'s supply scope becomes active and binding under the contract. May differ from the contract\'s own effective_start_date if the IMP is added via a change order.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this IMP\'s supply scope expires under the contract. May differ from the contract\'s effective_end_date if the IMP is removed or replaced via a change order.']
  supply_role varchar [note: 'The functional role this IMP plays within the study as defined in the contract scope: IMP (the investigational product under study), COMPARATOR (active reference drug), PLACEBO, RESCUE_MEDICATION, or AUXILIARY. This role is specific to the IMP-contract pairing and cannot reside on imp_master (which is study-agnostic) or study_contract (which is not IMP-specific).']
  unit_price decimal [note: 'The negotiated price per dispensing unit for this IMP under this specific contract. Belongs to the relationship because the same IMP may be priced differently across different study contracts or sponsors.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between imp_master and study_contract. It captures the specific terms under which a given investigational medicinal product is included in the supply scope of a Clinical Trial Agreement — recording the supply role, contracted quantity, unit price, and validity window for each IMP-contract pairing. Each record links one imp_master to one study_contract with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual supply relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single IMP (e.g., a novel oncology compound) is routinely supplied across multiple study contracts — different studies, different sponsors, different CROs — while a single study contract (CTA) almost always covers multiple IMPs: the investigational product, an active comparator, and a placebo. The business actively manages this relationship as a \'contracted supply item\' or \'IMP supply scope\' within each CTA, tracking contracted quantities, unit pricing, and the supply role (IMP vs. comparator vs. placebo) per IMP per contract. This is not derivable from transactional data; it is an operational record that procurement and supply chain teams create, negotiate, and update throughout the contract lifecycle.'
}

Table supply.imp_authorization {
  imp_authorization_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the imp_authorization association']
  clinical_trial_authorization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Clinical Trial Authorization under which this IMP is authorized.']
  imp_master_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the investigational medicinal product master record that is authorized under this CTA.']
  authorization_status_at_time timestamp [note: 'The authorization status of this specific IMP under this specific CTA at the time of record. Distinct from the overall CTA status, as individual IMPs within a multi-IMP CTA may have different authorization states (e.g., one IMP suspended while others remain authorized).']
  authorized_quantity decimal [note: 'The quantity of the IMP authorized for use under this specific CTA, as approved by the national competent authority. Belongs to the IMP-CTA pairing, not to either entity alone, as the same IMP may have different authorized quantities under different CTAs.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'The date from which this IMP is legally authorized for use under this CTA in the specified member state. May differ from the CTA\'s overall effective_from_date when IMPs are added via substantial modification.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'The date on which this IMP\'s authorization under this CTA expires or is terminated in the specified member state. Supports supply planning cutoff calculations and regulatory compliance monitoring.']
  imp_eudra_ct_number varchar [note: 'EudraCT or EudraGMDP reference number for the investigational medicinal product as registered in the EU regulatory system. Used to cross-reference IMP manufacturing and quality data with the CTA. [Moved from clinical_trial_authorization: This EudraCT/EudraGMDP reference for the IMP is a relationship-level identifier that belongs to the IMP-CTA pairing, not to the CTA alone. In a multi-IMP CTA, each IMP has its own EudraCT product number. Moving it to the association correctly models the per-IMP-per-CTA granularity.]']
  imp_name varchar [note: 'Name of the investigational medicinal product (IMP) covered by this Clinical Trial Authorization. Identifies the drug or biologic under investigation as declared in the CTA application dossier. [Moved from clinical_trial_authorization: This denormalized text field on clinical_trial_authorization was a workaround for the absence of a proper IMP-CTA association. With imp_authorization in place, the IMP identity is captured via the FK to imp_master, making this redundant text field unnecessary on the CTA record.]']
  member_state_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 country code of the EU member state or non-EU jurisdiction in which this IMP is authorized under this CTA. Captures the jurisdiction-specific nature of the IMP-CTA authorization pairing.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory authorization contract between an investigational medicinal product (imp_master) and a Clinical Trial Authorization (clinical_trial_authorization). It captures the specific terms under which a given IMP is authorized for use within a given CTA in a given EU member state jurisdiction, including authorized quantities, effective dates, and authorization status at the IMP level. Each record links one imp_master to one clinical_trial_authorization with attributes that exist only in the context of this IMP-CTA regulatory pairing, supporting EU CTR 536/2014 compliance and multi-country supply planning.. Existence Justification: In EU clinical trial operations, a single IMP (e.g., a monoclonal antibody) requires separate CTAs filed in each EU member state where the trial runs, meaning one IMP is covered by many CTAs. Conversely, a single CTA for a combination product or multi-arm trial can authorize multiple IMPs simultaneously. The business actively manages this relationship as a regulatory compliance record — tracking authorized quantities, effective dates, and authorization status per IMP-per-CTA combination — which is a named concept in EU CTR 536/2014 regulatory practice.'
}

Table supply.depot_sla_coverage {
  depot_sla_coverage_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the depot_sla_coverage association']
  depot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the clinical supply depot that is governed by the associated SLA.']
  service_level_agreement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Service Level Agreement that governs the associated depot.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which this SLA became binding and performance measurement began for this specific depot. Distinct from the SLA\'s own effective_start_date, which governs the SLA globally; this date governs when the SLA was applied to this particular depot.']
  last_review_date date [note: 'The most recent date on which this depot-SLA assignment was formally reviewed by supply chain governance. Drives scheduling of the next review and supports audit trail requirements.']
  performance_status varchar [note: 'Current compliance state of this depot against this SLA. Reflects whether the depot is meeting, breaching, or at-risk for the SLA threshold. Belongs to the assignment, not to the depot or SLA alone.']
  sla_scope varchar [note: 'Describes which activities, shipment types, or operational processes at this depot are covered by this SLA assignment (e.g., \'outbound IMP dispatch only\', \'all temperature-controlled storage operations\'). Scope may differ per depot even for the same SLA.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract/Assignment between a clinical supply depot and a Service Level Agreement. It captures which SLAs are actively governing each depot in the supply network, along with the operational details of that coverage — effective date, scope of activities covered, current performance status, and last review date. Each record links one depot to one SLA and holds attributes that exist only in the context of that specific depot-SLA assignment, enabling supply chain managers to audit compliance and manage SLA coverage across the depot network.. Existence Justification: In clinical trial supply operations, a depot (warehouse node) can be governed by multiple SLAs simultaneously — e.g., a temperature monitoring SLA, a dispatch turnaround SLA, and a receipt confirmation SLA — while a single SLA (e.g., \'dispatch within 24 hours\') can apply to multiple depots across the supply network. This is an operationally managed relationship: supply chain managers actively assign, activate, and review which SLAs govern each depot, and the assignment itself carries meaningful data (effective date, scope, performance status, last review date) that belongs to neither the depot nor the SLA alone. Business stakeholders in clinical supply would recognize this as \'Depot SLA Coverage\' or a \'Depot SLA Assignment\' — a governed, auditable record of which performance commitments apply to which supply nodes.'

Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single IMP (e.g., a cold-chain biological IMP) is governed by multiple SOPs simultaneously — a storage SOP, a dispensing SOP, a destruction SOP, and a cold-chain SOP — each applying to that product in a distinct capacity. Conversely, a single SOP (e.g., a GMP dispensing SOP) applies to multiple IMPs across different studies. The business actively manages this applicability relationship through document control processes, tracking when each SOP became applicable to each IMP, in what role, and whether training is required for that specific IMP-SOP pairing.'

  monitoring_action_item_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow state of the action item lifecycle in Oracle Siebel CTMS. Overdue status is set automatically when the due date passes without closure. Closed status requires documented evidence of resolution.']

  recurrence_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this action item represents a recurring finding previously identified at the same site or study. Recurring findings may trigger escalation to a formal CAPA workflow and are tracked for site performance risk scoring.']
  regulatory_impact varchar [note: 'Assessment of the potential regulatory impact of the finding underlying this action item.   response_date date [note: 'Date on which the site formally submitted their response to the action item. Used to measure site responsiveness KPIs and to determine whether the response was received within the required timeframe.']
  response_text varchar [note: 'Formal written response provided by the site (PI or CRC) acknowledging the action item and describing the planned or completed corrective actions. Captured in Oracle Siebel CTMS as part of the action item resolution workflow.']
  responsible_party_role varchar [note: 'Functional role category of the party accountable for resolving the action item. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: site_staff|cra|sponsor|pi|crc|data_management|safety — promote to reference product]']
  source_type varchar [note: 'Identifies the originating activity or process that generated this action item (e.g., on-site monitoring visit, remote monitoring review, SDV finding, protocol deviation, safety signal, audit). Supports risk-based monitoring (RBM) analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: on_site_visit|remote_monitoring|sdv_review|protocol_deviation|safety_signal|audit|sponsor_review — promote to reference product]']
  subject_safety_impact boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the finding underlying this action item has a direct or potential impact on subject safety. When True, triggers expedited review by the medical monitor and may require safety reporting obligations per ICH E2A.']
  title varchar [note: 'Short, descriptive title summarizing the action item finding or required corrective action. Used as the primary display label in CTMS dashboards, monitoring visit reports, and escalation notifications.']
  verification_method varchar [note: 'Method used by the CRA or monitor to verify that the corrective action was implemented and the action item can be closed (e.g., SDV, document review, on-site visit, remote review). Supports GCP audit trail requirements.']

  Note: 'Formal action item raised as a result of a monitoring finding, protocol deviation, or escalation trigger. Tracks action description, responsible party (site staff, CRA, or sponsor), due date, priority level, current status (open, in-progress, overdue, closed), escalation flag, and closure confirmation with evidence. Managed in Oracle Siebel CTMS with automated escalation workflows for overdue items. Primary operational entity for site performance management, regulatory inspection readiness, and GCP compliance tracking.'

  computed_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'Current computed numeric value of the KRI for the associated site, derived from the source system data as of the last computation run. This is the principal quantitative fact of the risk indicator record.']

  effective_until date [note: 'Date on which this KRI definition was superseded or retired. Null for currently active KRI definitions. Supports historical analysis and monitoring plan amendment tracking.']

  indicator_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the KRI as defined in the RBM monitoring plan (e.g., \'Screen Failure Rate\', \'Missing Data Rate\', \'SAE Reporting Timeliness\'). Used in dashboards, monitoring visit reports, and sponsor communications.']
  indicator_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the KRI definition within the monitoring plan. Active KRIs are computed and monitored; draft KRIs are under review; retired KRIs are no longer in use.']
  indicator_type varchar [note: 'Quantitative type of the KRI value, indicating whether the computed metric is a rate, absolute count, percentage, ratio, or duration in days. Governs how the value is interpreted against thresholds.']
  is_centralized_monitoring boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this KRI is part of the Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) program, as opposed to a site-level operational indicator. Supports differentiation of CSM KRIs from operational monitoring metrics.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for CRA or data manager annotations regarding the KRI computation, alert status, or remediation context. Supports monitoring visit report narrative and sponsor communication.']
  numerator_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'Raw numerator component of the KRI computation (e.g., number of screen failures, number of missing data points, number of overdue SAE reports). Stored to support audit and recomputation validation.']
  prior_computed_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'KRI computed value from the immediately preceding computation cycle for the same site. Enables trend analysis and detection of rapid deterioration or improvement in site risk profile.']
  red_threshold decimal(18,4) [note: 'Numeric threshold value at which the KRI triggers a red (critical) alert, indicating a significant risk requiring immediate escalation and corrective action per the RBM monitoring plan.']
  reference_period_end date [note: 'End date of the data window used to compute the KRI value. Together with reference_period_start, defines the exact temporal scope of the KRI computation for reproducibility and audit.']
  reference_period_start date [note: 'Start date of the data window used to compute the KRI value (e.g., rolling 30-day window start, or study start date for cumulative KRIs). Defines the temporal scope of the computation.']
  risk_indicator_category varchar [note: 'Business category classifying the domain of risk the KRI monitors. Supports stratified risk reporting across enrollment, data quality, safety, protocol compliance, and Investigational Product (IP) accountability domains.']
  risk_score_contribution decimal(5,2) [note: 'Weighted contribution of this KRI to the overall site risk score, expressed as a percentage (0–100). Reflects the KRI\'s relative importance in the composite site risk scoring model.']
  sdv_impact varchar [note: 'Defines the impact of this KRI\'s alert status on the Source Data Verification (SDV) strategy for the site. A red alert may trigger targeted or increased SDV; a green status may support reduced SDV per the risk-adaptive monitoring plan.']
  sponsor_defined boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this KRI was defined by the sponsor (True) or by the CRO as part of its standard RBM methodology (False). Supports differentiation of sponsor-mandated versus CRO-standard risk indicators.']
  threshold_direction varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the KRI alert is triggered when the computed value exceeds (above) or falls below (below) the defined amber/red thresholds. Critical for correct alert logic in centralized statistical monitoring (CSM).']
  trend_direction varchar [note: 'Directional trend of the KRI value compared to the prior computation cycle. Supports proactive risk management by identifying sites where risk is worsening before threshold breach.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Unit in which the KRI value and thresholds are expressed (e.g., \'%\', \'days\', \'count\', \'ratio\'). Ensures consistent interpretation of computed values across sites and studies.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this KRI record, supporting change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the KRI definition (e.g., v1.0, v2.1), incremented when the calculation method, thresholds, or data source is amended. Supports audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  weight decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric weight assigned to this KRI in the composite site risk scoring model, reflecting its relative importance compared to other KRIs in the monitoring plan. Used in weighted risk score calculations.']

  Note: 'Centralized monitoring risk indicator (also known as Key Risk Indicator or KRI) defined within the RBM monitoring plan. Captures indicator name, category (enrollment, data quality, safety, protocol compliance, IP accountability), calculation method, threshold values (amber/red), data source, and current computed value per site. Supports centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) and site risk scoring in the RBM framework.'
}
