  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this unblinding request originated. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements in the lakehouse silver layer.']
  source_system_request_code varchar [note: 'The native identifier of this unblinding request in the originating operational system (Oracle Clinical One or Medidata Rave RTSM). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracing in the lakehouse.']
  sponsor_notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the study sponsor was formally notified of the unblinding event. Required for emergency unblinding events per GCP and sponsor agreements. Null if not yet notified.']
  submitted_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the unblinding request was formally submitted by the requestor in the RTSM/IRT system.   treatment_arm_revealed varchar [note: 'The treatment arm or randomization code revealed upon approved unblinding (e.g., \'Active Drug A 10mg\', \'Placebo\', \'Comparator B\'). Populated only when final_outcome is \'approved\'. Highly sensitive as it compromises blinding integrity for the subject. Restricted to authorized personnel only.']
  unblinding_reason varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the clinical or regulatory justification for the unblinding request. Drives urgency classification and approval routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sae_medical_emergency|regulatory_requirement|dsmb_interim_analysis|database_lock|planned_unblinding|other — promote to reference product]']
  unblinding_scope varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the unblinding request pertains to a single subject (emergency or medical necessity) or to the entire study (planned events such as Database Lock, interim analysis, or final analysis).']
  unblinding_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the treatment assignment was actually revealed to the authorized recipient. Null if the request was rejected or withdrawn. Critical for GCP audit trail and regulatory reporting timelines.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this unblinding request record was most recently modified in the lakehouse silver layer. Tracks the latest state change for audit trail and data quality monitoring.']
  urgency_level varchar [note: 'Clinical urgency classification of the unblinding request. Emergency indicates immediate patient safety risk requiring unblinding within hours; urgent indicates within 24 hours; routine indicates planned/scheduled unblinding with no immediate safety concern.']
  withdrawal_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation provided by the requestor when withdrawing an unblinding request before final resolution. Null when the request was not withdrawn. Required for audit trail completeness.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a request to unblind a subject\'s treatment assignment, encompassing the full request-through-resolution lifecycle including multi-level approval steps. Captures requestor identity, requestor role, clinical justification (SAE, medical emergency, regulatory requirement, planned DBL unblinding, interim analysis), urgency level, request timestamp, approval chain (approver identity, role, decision, rationale, conditions, timestamp per approval step), final outcome (approved/rejected/escalated), unblinding timestamp, and the unblinded treatment arm revealed. Covers both emergency single-subject unblinding and planned study-level unblinding events. Critical for GCP compliance, 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail, and DSMB/DMC oversight. Sourced from Oracle Clinical One and Medidata Rave RTSM.'
}

  dmc_charter_version varchar [note: 'Version of the DMC/DSMB charter under which this unblinded package was prepared and reviewed, ensuring compliance with the agreed operating procedures.']
  dsmb_recommendation varchar [note: 'Formal recommendation issued by the DSMB/DMC following review of this unblinded package. Drives subsequent study management decisions by the sponsor.']
  encryption_method varchar [note: 'Encryption standard applied to the unblinded data package to protect blinding integrity during transmission and storage.']
  interim_analysis_number varchar [note: 'Sequential number of the interim analysis associated with this unblinded package (e.g., 1 for first interim, 2 for second interim). Aligns with the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) interim analysis schedule.']
  meeting_date date [note: 'Scheduled or actual date of the DSMB/DMC meeting for which this unblinded data package was prepared.']
  package_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable unique reference code for the unblinded data package, typically formatted as DSMB-{StudyCode}-{Year}-V{Version}. Used for tracking and audit trail purposes across systems.']
  package_location_uri varchar [note: 'Secure URI or vault path where the unblinded data package is stored in the eTMF or secure document repository (e.g., Veeva Vault). Access is restricted to authorized unblinded personnel only.']
  package_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing any additional notes, caveats, or contextual information about this unblinded data package, such as known data quality issues or deviations from the SAP.']
  package_prepared_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the unblinded data package was finalized and locked for delivery to the DSMB. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this transaction.']
  package_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the DSMB unblinded data package. Tracks progression from preparation through delivery, review, and post-meeting destruction. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|finalized|delivered|received|under_review|destroyed|superseded — promote to reference product]']
  package_version varchar [note: 'Sequential version number of the unblinded data package for a given DSMB meeting. Incremented when a corrected or supplemental package is issued prior to or after the meeting.']
  receipt_confirmed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the DSMB/DMC has formally confirmed receipt of the unblinded data package prior to the meeting.']
  receipt_confirmed_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the DSMB/DMC member or designated representative who confirmed receipt of the unblinded package.']
  receipt_confirmed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the DSMB/DMC formally confirmed receipt of the unblinded data package.']
  recommendation_date date [note: 'Date on which the DSMB/DMC issued its formal recommendation following review of the unblinded data package.']
  sae_count varchar [note: 'Total number of Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) reported as of the data cut-off date, included in the unblinded safety summary for DSMB review.']
  sap_version_reference varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) that governed the interim analysis included in this unblinded package.']
  sponsor_notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the sponsor was formally notified of the DSMB/DMC recommendation.']
  sponsor_notified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the sponsor has been formally notified of the DSMB/DMC recommendation following the meeting.']
  stopping_rule_triggered boolean [note: 'Indicates whether any pre-specified stopping rule (for safety, efficacy, or futility) was triggered based on the interim analysis results in this unblinded package.']
  subjects_enrolled_count varchar [note: 'Total number of subjects enrolled in the study as of the data cut-off date, included in this unblinded package for DSMB review.']
  subjects_evaluable_count varchar [note: 'Number of subjects with sufficient data to be included in the interim analysis population (e.g., Intent-to-Treat or Per Protocol population) as of the data cut-off date.']
  treatment_arm_labels_included varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of unblinded treatment arm labels (e.g., \'Drug A 10mg, Drug A 20mg, Placebo\') included in this package. Captures which arms were unblinded for the DSMB review.']
  unblinded_statistician_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the independent unblinded statistician who prepared the interim analysis. Captured for audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  unblinded_statistician_org varchar [note: 'Name of the organization or CRO unit to which the unblinded statistician belongs, confirming independence from the blinded study team and sponsor.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this DSMB unblinded package record was last modified in the system.']

  Note: 'Manages the preparation and delivery of unblinded data packages to the DSMB (Data Safety Monitoring Board) or DMC (Data Monitoring Committee). Captures package version, meeting date, unblinded statistician identity, data cut-off date, treatment arm labels included, delivery method, receipt confirmation, and destruction confirmation post-meeting. Ensures controlled unblinded data access for interim safety reviews.'
}

  consolidation_scope varchar [note: 'Indicates how the child organization\'s financials are consolidated into the parent\'s financial statements per IFRS 10 / US GAAP ASC 810.   contracting_entity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the child organization is authorized to independently execute clinical trial contracts and CRO agreements on behalf of the sponsor corporate family.   hierarchy_level varchar [note: 'Numeric depth level of the child organization within the corporate hierarchy tree. Level 1 represents a direct subsidiary of the ultimate parent; higher values indicate deeper nesting. Enables efficient tree traversal and roll-up aggregation across sponsor corporate families.']
  hierarchy_path varchar [note: 'Materialized path string representing the full ancestry chain from the ultimate parent to the child organization, using a delimiter-separated list of organization IDs (e.g., \'1001/1045/1078\'). Enables efficient subtree queries and hierarchy visualization without recursive joins.']
  hierarchy_version varchar [note: 'Monotonically incrementing version number for this hierarchy relationship record, supporting optimistic concurrency control and change history tracking. Incremented each time the relationship attributes are updated.']
  ind_holder_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the child organization holds or co-holds an Investigational New Drug (IND) application or equivalent regulatory authorization (e.g., CTA in EU) in its own name. Relevant for regulatory accountability and submission ownership tracking.']
  is_controlling_entity boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the parent organization exercises control over the child organization as defined by IFRS 10 (power over investee, exposure to variable returns, ability to use power to affect returns). True = controlling; False = non-controlling interest.']
  is_primary_path boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this relationship represents the primary (canonical) reporting path for the child organization when multiple parent relationships exist (e.g., matrix structures or dual-reporting affiliates). True = primary path used for standard roll-up; False = secondary or alternate path.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional contextual information about the organizational hierarchy relationship not captured in structured fields (e.g., special contractual arrangements, regulatory carve-outs, transition notes during M&A activity).']
  ownership_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of equity ownership held by the parent organization in the child organization, expressed as a decimal value between 0.00 and 100.00. Critical for determining consolidation thresholds under IFRS 10 and for sponsor financial roll-up reporting. Classified confidential as it reflects proprietary corporate financial structure.']
  pipeline_scope varchar [note: 'Defines the breadth of the sponsor\'s drug development pipeline that the child organization is responsible for managing or contracting. Supports portfolio analytics and CRO engagement planning across the sponsor corporate family.']
  regulatory_jurisdiction varchar [note: 'Primary regulatory authority governing the child organization\'s clinical trial activities (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA, TGA, MHRA, Health Canada). Determines applicable regulatory submission requirements and GCP compliance frameworks for studies contracted through this entity.']
  relationship_basis varchar [note: 'The legal or operational basis underpinning the parent-child relationship. Equity = share ownership; Contractual = agreement-based control without equity; Regulatory = regulatory-mandated grouping; Operational = functional reporting without legal ownership; Statutory = legally mandated structure.']
  relationship_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this hierarchy relationship, used for cross-system referencing in Oracle Siebel CTMS, SAP S/4HANA, and regulatory submissions. Follows the sponsor organization\'s internal coding convention.']
  relationship_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the parent-child organizational relationship. Drives whether the relationship is included in active roll-up reporting and sponsor portfolio consolidation.']
  relationship_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the corporate relationship between the parent and child organization. Drives roll-up logic and reporting scope. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: parent|subsidiary|affiliate|division|joint_venture|licensee|branch|representative_office — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]']
  sap_company_code varchar [note: 'Four-character SAP S/4HANA company code assigned to the child organization for financial accounting, accounts payable/receivable, and project accounting. Enables direct linkage between the organizational hierarchy and financial ledger entries in SAP S/4HANA.']
  source_record_reference varchar [note: 'Native record identifier from the source operational system (e.g., Siebel CTMS account relationship ID, SAP company code pairing key). Enables reverse traceability from the Silver Layer back to the originating system record for reconciliation and audit.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this hierarchy relationship record was sourced or last updated. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across Oracle Siebel CTMS, SAP S/4HANA, Workday HCM, and Veeva Vault.']
  therapeutic_area_alignment varchar [note: 'Primary therapeutic area(s) for which the child organization is responsible within the sponsor corporate family (e.g., Oncology, Cardiovascular, Neuroscience, Immunology). Supports portfolio roll-up reporting and pipeline analysis by therapeutic area across the sponsor hierarchy.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this organizational hierarchy relationship record was most recently modified in the Silver Layer data product. Supports change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail requirements.']
  veeva_account_code varchar [note: 'Unique identifier for the child organization\'s account record in Veeva Vault, used for eTMF document ownership, regulatory submission tracking, and quality management linkage. Supports traceability between the corporate hierarchy and document management.']
  voting_rights_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of voting rights held by the parent organization in the child organization. May differ from ownership percentage in cases of dual-class share structures or contractual voting arrangements. Relevant for regulatory filings and control determination under IFRS 10.']

  Note: 'Defines parent-child corporate hierarchy relationships among sponsor organizations, capturing subsidiary, affiliate, and division structures. Tracks relationship type (parent, subsidiary, affiliate, division, joint-venture), effective dates, ownership percentage, controlling entity flag, and hierarchy depth level. Enables roll-up reporting across sponsor corporate families and supports multi-national sponsor structures where regional entities contract independently.'
}

  phase_start_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the pipeline asset formally entered this development phase. For Phase I, this typically aligns with first-in-human (FIH) dosing; for NDA/BLA, with submission filing date.']

  planned_phase_end_date date [note: 'Originally planned calendar date for the pipeline asset to complete this development phase. Used to measure schedule variance and forecast downstream phase timelines.']
  planned_phase_start_date date [note: 'Originally planned calendar date for the pipeline asset to enter this development phase, as defined in the integrated development plan. Used to measure schedule variance against actual start.']
  previous_phase_code varchar [note: 'Phase code of the immediately preceding development phase for this pipeline asset. Enables direct traversal of the phase history chain without requiring a self-join. Null for the first phase record.']
  primary_endpoint_met boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the primary efficacy or safety endpoint defined for this development phase was met upon phase completion. True = primary endpoint achieved; False = not achieved; Null = phase not yet completed or endpoint not yet evaluated.']
  regulatory_milestone_achieved varchar [note: 'Description of the key regulatory milestone achieved upon completion or during this phase (e.g., \'IND Clearance\', \'End-of-Phase-II Meeting\', \'NDA Acceptance\', \'Breakthrough Therapy Designation\'). Null if no milestone was achieved.']
  regulatory_milestone_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the regulatory milestone associated with this phase was formally achieved or received. Used for regulatory timeline tracking and submission planning.']
  regulatory_strategy_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field capturing the sponsor\'s regulatory strategy for this phase, including planned agency interactions, submission strategy, and any special regulatory considerations. Classified as confidential due to commercially sensitive strategic content.']
  study_count varchar [note: 'Number of clinical studies (protocols) conducted under this pipeline asset phase. Provides a measure of the breadth of evidence generation within the phase.']
  termination_reason_category varchar [note: 'Standardized category for the primary reason a phase was terminated. Enables portfolio-level analysis of attrition drivers across the development pipeline. Null if phase was not terminated.']
  transition_reason varchar [note: 'Narrative explanation for why the pipeline asset transitioned into or out of this development phase. Captures scientific, regulatory, commercial, or safety rationale for phase progression, hold, or termination.']
  transition_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the type of phase transition event. Distinguishes between forward progression, temporary hold, full termination, restart after hold, or protocol amendment-driven transition.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this pipeline asset phase record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.']

  Note: 'Tracks the development phase history and transitions of a pipeline asset across its lifecycle. Captures phase (preclinical, Phase I, Phase Ib, Phase II, Phase IIa, Phase IIb, Phase III, Phase IV, NDA/BLA submission, approved), phase start date, phase end date, phase status (active, completed, on-hold, terminated), regulatory milestone achieved, and reason for phase transition or termination. Provides a longitudinal view of asset progression through the clinical development continuum.'
}

  plan_name varchar [note: 'Descriptive name of the strategic account plan, typically including the sponsor name and plan period (e.g., \'Pfizer Strategic Account Plan FY2025\').']
  plan_start_date date [note: 'Date on which the account plan period formally begins and strategic objectives become active. Aligns with the sponsor engagement cycle or CRO fiscal year.']
  plan_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the account plan. Draft: being authored; Under Review: submitted for internal approval; Approved: signed off by leadership; Active: currently being executed; Closed: plan period ended or superseded.']
  plan_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the account plan by its temporal scope and purpose. Annual plans cover a single fiscal year; multi-year plans span two or more years; renewal plans are created at contract renewal; remediation plans address relationship recovery.']
  plan_version varchar [note: 'Version number of this account plan document, incremented each time the plan is formally revised and re-approved. Supports plan lifecycle tracking and audit trail.']
  plan_year varchar [note: 'Primary fiscal or calendar year this account plan covers. For multi-year plans, this represents the starting year. Used for annual performance tracking and year-over-year comparison.']
  preferred_provider_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the CRO\'s preferred or approved provider designation with this sponsor. Preferred status typically grants first-look rights on new study opportunities and streamlined contracting.']
  regulatory_affairs_revenue_target_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Revenue target in USD for regulatory affairs service line (IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions, eCTD preparation, agency interactions) within this account plan period.']
  relationship_development_goals varchar [note: 'Specific goals for deepening or broadening the CRO-sponsor relationship during the plan period, such as expanding into new divisions, achieving executive-level engagement, or establishing a joint innovation council.']
  relationship_health_score varchar [note: 'Numeric score (1-10) representing the assessed health and strength of the CRO-sponsor relationship at the time of plan creation or last review. Informed by sponsor satisfaction surveys, escalation history, and account manager assessment.']
  revenue_target_currency varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the revenue target amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Supports multi-currency sponsor relationships.']
  revenue_target_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total CRO revenue target in US dollars for this account plan period across all service lines. Represents the gross contracted and pipeline revenue goal set during account planning.']
  risk_summary varchar [note: 'Summary of key risks to the account relationship or revenue targets identified during plan development, such as sponsor M&A activity, pipeline failures, budget cuts, or competitive displacement. Informs mitigation planning.']
  sponsor_satisfaction_score decimal(4,2) [note: 'Most recent sponsor satisfaction survey score (e.g., on a 1.00–5.00 or 0.00–10.00 scale) captured from formal sponsor feedback mechanisms. Baseline metric for relationship development goals in the plan.']
  strategic_objectives varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the primary strategic objectives for this account plan period, such as expanding into new therapeutic areas, securing preferred provider status, or deepening data analytics partnerships. Free-text field capturing the overarching relationship strategy.']

  Note: 'Strategic account plan developed by the CRO for key sponsor accounts, capturing the annual or multi-year relationship strategy. Tracks plan period, strategic objectives, revenue targets by service line, pipeline opportunities identified, relationship development goals, competitive threats, key sponsor stakeholders to engage, planned governance touchpoints, and plan status (draft, approved, active, closed). Drives proactive account management and business development activities for strategic sponsor relationships.'

Table sponsor.engagement_contact_assignment {
  engagement_contact_assignment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the engagement_contact_assignment association']
  sponsor_contact_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this assignment record to the specific sponsor contact individual being assigned to the engagement.']
  sponsor_engagement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this assignment record to the specific CRO-sponsor commercial engagement to which the contact is assigned.']
  assignment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this contact\'s assignment within this specific engagement. Corresponds to contact_status_in_engagement identified in the detection phase. A contact may be active in one engagement and departed from another simultaneously.']
  end_date date [note: 'The date on which this sponsor contact\'s involvement in this specific engagement formally ended or is scheduled to end. Moved from sponsor_contact.engagement_end_date, where it was incorrectly scoped globally.']
  engagement_end_date date [note: 'The date on which this sponsor contact\'s engagement with the CRO formally ended (e.g., upon departure from sponsor, study close-out, or contract termination). Null for currently active contacts. [Moved from sponsor_contact: Same rationale as engagement_start_date — this is an assignment-level date, not a contact-level attribute. Moving it to the association correctly captures when the contact\'s involvement in each specific engagement ended.]']
  engagement_start_date date [note: 'The date on which this sponsor contact formally began their engagement with the CRO, typically aligned with contract execution or study assignment. Used for relationship tenure tracking and access provisioning. [Moved from sponsor_contact: This date is scoped to a specific contact-engagement assignment, not to the contact globally. A contact serving multiple engagements has a different start date per engagement. Retaining it on sponsor_contact forces a 1:N assumption and loses per-engagement precision.]']
  is_primary boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this contact is the designated primary point of contact for this specific engagement. A contact may be primary in one engagement and secondary in another; this flag belongs to the assignment, not to the contact record globally. Replaces the global is_primary_contact flag on sponsor_contact for engagement-scoped use.']
  role_in_engagement varchar [note: 'The functional role this sponsor contact holds within this specific engagement. A contact may hold different roles across different engagements (e.g., medical monitor in one, regulatory lead in another). This attribute belongs to the assignment, not to the contact or engagement globally.']
  start_date date [note: 'The date on which this sponsor contact formally began their involvement in this specific engagement. Moved from sponsor_contact.engagement_start_date, where it was incorrectly scoped to the contact globally rather than per engagement assignment.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal Role assignment between a sponsor_contact and an engagement. It captures the operational record of which sponsor personnel are assigned to a CRO commercial engagement, in what functional capacity, and for what period. Each record links one sponsor_contact to one engagement with attributes — role, effective dates, primary flag, and status — that exist only in the context of this specific assignment and cannot correctly reside on either the contact or the engagement alone.. Existence Justification: In CRO operations, sponsor contacts are formally assigned to commercial engagements in specific roles (medical monitor, project manager, regulatory lead, financial approver). A single contact — such as a VP of Clinical Operations — routinely spans multiple engagements simultaneously, and each engagement requires multiple contacts across different functional roles. The business actively manages these assignments as named records with effective dates, role designations, and primary-contact flags that belong to neither the contact nor the engagement alone.'
}

Table sponsor.engagement_scope {
  engagement_scope_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the engagement_scope association']
  health_authority_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the health authority that is in scope for this engagement']
  sponsor_engagement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the CRO-sponsor commercial engagement that defines the scope context']
  engagement_scope_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this health authority\'s scope within the engagement (e.g., planned, active, suspended, closed). Sourced from detection phase relationship data as engagement_status.']
  primary_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the designated primary regulatory contact at this health authority for this specific engagement. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  regulatory_region varchar [note: 'The specific regulatory region or jurisdiction agreed as in-scope for this engagement-HA pairing (e.g., North America, EU, Asia-Pacific). Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  submission_volume_target decimal [note: 'The planned number or volume of regulatory submissions to this health authority under this engagement for the planning period. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract/Scope between a sponsor engagement and a health authority. It captures the formal designation of which health authorities are in scope for a given CRO-sponsor engagement, along with submission volume targets, regional scope, and designated regulatory contacts agreed for that pairing. Each record links one engagement to one health authority with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific engagement-HA relationship and cannot reside on either entity alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical research CRO operations, a single sponsor engagement spans multiple regulatory jurisdictions simultaneously — a global Phase III trial under one engagement may require FDA, EMA, PMDA, and MHRA submissions concurrently. Conversely, a major health authority like the FDA is relevant to dozens of active sponsor engagements at any given time. The CRO actively manages which health authorities are in scope per engagement, tracks submission volume targets per HA per engagement, and assigns primary regulatory contacts — this is an operationally managed relationship, not a derived analytical correlation.'
}

Table agreement.obligation_fulfillment {
  obligation_fulfillment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the obligation_fulfillment association']
  contract_obligation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the contractual obligation being fulfilled by the associated deliverable']
  deliverable_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the contractually committed deliverable that fulfills or partially fulfills the obligation']
  evidence_document_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or URL to the document or artifact that serves as evidence of fulfillment for this specific deliverable-obligation pairing. Used in GCP audits and contract compliance reviews to demonstrate that the obligation was met.']
  fulfillment_date date [note: 'The date on which this deliverable was formally accepted as fulfilling this specific contractual obligation. Belongs to the association because the same deliverable may fulfill different obligations on different dates depending on sponsor review timelines.']
  fulfillment_percentage decimal [note: 'Numeric percentage (0–100) indicating the degree to which this deliverable satisfies the associated obligation. Supports partial fulfillment scenarios where an obligation requires multiple deliverables collectively, each contributing a portion of the total fulfillment.']
  fulfillment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this specific deliverable-to-obligation fulfillment link. Tracks whether the deliverable has been accepted as satisfying this obligation, is pending review, or has been rejected as insufficient evidence of fulfillment.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the fulfillment event between a contractual deliverable and a contract obligation. It captures the operational record of how and to what degree a specific deliverable satisfies a specific contractual obligation, serving as the system of record for GCP audit trails, contract compliance reporting, and dispute resolution. Each record links one deliverable to one contract_obligation with attributes that exist only in the context of this fulfillment relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical research contract management, a single deliverable (e.g., a Clinical Study Report) can fulfill multiple contractual obligations simultaneously (e.g., a regulatory reporting obligation AND a financial milestone obligation AND an operational reporting obligation), while a single contractual obligation (e.g., \'Submit all required regulatory documents\') can be satisfied by multiple deliverables. CROs actively manage this mapping as \'obligation fulfillment tracking\' — a recognized compliance and audit process where each deliverable-obligation link carries its own fulfillment status, evidence, and completion date. This is not an analytical correlation; it is an operationally managed record created, updated, and closed by contract managers and compliance teams during study execution.'
}

  initial_filing_date date [note: 'Date the application was first submitted to the health authority. For INDs, this is the date the IND package was received by FDA. For NDAs/BLAs, this is the date of original submission. This is the principal BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this entity.']
  lead_agency varchar [note: 'Primary regulatory health authority to which this application is filed. Determines the regulatory pathway, submission format, and review timelines applicable to this dossier. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|Health Canada|TGA|ANVISA|NMPA|Other — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  lifecycle_phase varchar [note: 'Current development phase associated with this regulatory application. Tracks the application from pre-IND through post-approval lifecycle. Supports portfolio planning and regulatory strategy alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pre_ind|phase_1|phase_2|phase_3|nda_bla_maa|post_approval|discontinued — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing additional regulatory context, strategic notes, or agency-specific instructions not captured in structured fields. Used by regulatory affairs teams for internal documentation.']
  orphan_drug_designation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the FDA Office of Orphan Products Development (OOPD) or EMA Committee for Orphan Medicinal Products (COMP) has granted Orphan Drug Designation for this application. Confers 7-year market exclusivity (FDA) or 10-year (EMA) and fee waivers.']
  pdufa_goal_date date [note: 'FDA-assigned PDUFA action date by which the agency commits to completing its review of an NDA or BLA. Applicable only to marketing applications under PDUFA. Drives internal milestone planning and commercial readiness timelines.']
  priority_review boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the FDA has granted Priority Review designation to this NDA or BLA, reducing the standard review clock from 12 months to 6 months. Applicable to drugs offering major advances in treatment or providing treatment where no adequate therapy exists.']
  product_name varchar [note: 'Name of the drug, biologic, or device covered by this application. May be the INN (International Nonproprietary Name), proprietary brand name, or code name at the investigational stage.']
  product_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the investigational or approved product by modality. Determines the applicable regulatory pathway, CMC requirements, and review division assignment at the agency.']
  rolling_review boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the health authority has granted rolling review, allowing submission and review of completed sections of the dossier before the full application is submitted. Applicable under FDA Fast Track and EMA PRIME/rolling review procedures.']
  sponsor_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the sponsor\'s designated regulatory contact as listed on the application cover sheet (e.g., FDA Form 1571 for INDs). This individual is the official point of contact for agency communications.']
  submission_format varchar [note: 'Technical format used for dossier submission to the health authority. eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document) is the standard for FDA, EMA, PMDA; NeeS (Non-eCTD Electronic Submission) is a transitional format; paper submissions are legacy.']
  subtype varchar [note: 'Further classification within the application type. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Commercial|Research|Treatment|Emergency|505(b)(1)|505(b)(2)|505(j)|Original|Supplement|Efficacy Supplement — promote to reference product]']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Broad disease or medical specialty area covered by the application (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology, Infectious Disease, Immunology). Used for portfolio segmentation, resource allocation, and regulatory strategy reporting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this regulatory application record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  veeva_vault_dossier_reference varchar [note: 'Cross-reference identifier linking this application record to the corresponding eTMF/regulatory dossier in Veeva Vault (the system of record for regulatory submissions and document management). Enables traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the source system.']

  Note: 'Master record for regulatory applications (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, CTA, IMPD) filed with health authorities. Tracks application number, application type and subtype, therapeutic area, indication, sponsor reference, lead agency, application status (active, approved, withdrawn, refused), initial filing date, approval date, lifecycle phase, and type-specific attributes including IND number/type/annual report dates for investigational applications and PDUFA goal date/priority review/breakthrough therapy/orphan drug designations for marketing applications. Parent entity for all submissions, correspondence, approvals, and commitments under a given regulatory dossier. SSOT for the complete regulatory application lifecycle.'
}

  ectd_validation_warning_count varchar [note: 'Total number of non-critical technical validation warnings identified during eCTD validation of this submission sequence. Warnings do not block submission but must be reviewed and justified.']

  response_due_date date [note: 'Deadline by which the sponsor must submit a response to an agency information request or complete response letter associated with this submission sequence. Null if no response is required.']
  review_clock_start_date date [note: 'Date on which the regulatory authority\'s formal review clock begins for this submission sequence (e.g., PDUFA Day 1 for FDA, Day 0 for EMA). Derived from agency acknowledgement and used for PDUFA/review deadline tracking.']
  review_clock_target_date date [note: 'Target date by which the regulatory authority is expected to complete review of this submission sequence, calculated from the review clock start date per applicable PDUFA or EMA timelines. Critical for regulatory milestone planning.']
  sequence_number varchar [note: 'Four-digit zero-padded sequence number uniquely identifying this submission within the regulatory application lifecycle (e.g., 0000 for original, 0001 for first amendment).   submission_subtype varchar [note: 'Further classification of the submission type providing regulatory-specific granularity (e.g., Prior Approval Supplement, Changes Being Effected, Complete Response, Major Amendment, Minor Amendment). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: prior_approval_supplement|changes_being_effected|complete_response|major_amendment|minor_amendment|annual_report — promote to reference product]']
  submission_unit varchar [note: 'The specific regulatory submission unit or grouping within the eCTD backbone that this sequence belongs to (e.g., \'IND Safety Report\', \'NDA Module 5 Clinical Study Report\', \'BLA CMC Supplement\'). Aligns with Veeva Vault RIM submission unit taxonomy.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this submission sequence record, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+.']

  Note: 'Tracks individual eCTD submission sequences within a regulatory application. Each sequence has a sequence number, submission type (original, amendment, supplement, response, withdrawal), sequence date, eCTD lifecycle operation (new, replace, append, delete), CTD module scope, submission reason, and validation status (eCTD technical validation result). Enables granular tracking of dossier evolution over time.'
}

  dsmb_notification_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) must be notified of this protocol amendment, typically required for amendments affecting safety monitoring, stopping rules, or interim analysis plans.']
  ectd_sequence_number varchar [note: 'Sequence number assigned to the eCTD submission package containing this protocol amendment, as tracked in Veeva Vault regulatory submissions module. Enables traceability to the specific eCTD lifecycle submission.']
  ethics_approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the IRB/IEC granted approval for the protocol amendment. Required before implementation at sites under the jurisdiction of that ethics committee.']
  ethics_submission_date date [note: 'Date on which the protocol amendment was submitted to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) for review and approval.']
  global_submission_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this amendment was submitted simultaneously to multiple health authorities as part of a global regulatory strategy, requiring coordinated timelines across FDA, EMA, PMDA, and other agencies.']
  icf_version_impacted varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the Informed Consent Form (ICF) that must be updated as a result of this amendment. Links to the ICF version management workflow in Clinpal and the document management system.']
  implementation_date date [note: 'Date on which the protocol amendment was operationally implemented at clinical sites, including updated procedures, training, and revised eCRF forms in Medidata Rave. Must be on or after all required regulatory and ethics approvals.']
  planned_implementation_date date [note: 'Target date for operational implementation of the amendment at clinical sites, used for project planning and site readiness tracking in Oracle Siebel CTMS.']
  prior_approval_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this amendment requires prior approval from the health authority before implementation (true for substantial amendments) versus notification-only (false for non-substantial/administrative amendments).']
  reconsent_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether enrolled subjects must provide updated informed consent (ICF re-consent) as a result of this amendment. Triggers ICF version update workflow in Clinpal and site notification via Oracle Siebel CTMS.']
  review_deadline_date date [note: 'Calculated or mandated deadline by which the health authority must respond to the amendment submission per applicable regulations (e.g., 30-day FDA IND amendment review window, EMA assessment timeline). Used for escalation and follow-up tracking.']
  safety_impact_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the protocol amendment has a direct impact on subject safety, risk-benefit profile, or safety monitoring procedures. Triggers expedited regulatory review and DSMB/DMC notification requirements.']
  site_notification_date date [note: 'Date on which clinical sites were formally notified of the approved protocol amendment and required to begin implementation, including updated training and revised procedures. Tracked in Oracle Siebel CTMS.']
  sponsor_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the sponsor or CRO regulatory affairs contact responsible for preparing and submitting this protocol amendment. Used for regulatory correspondence tracking.']
  subject_impact_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the amendment affects subjects currently enrolled in the study, requiring re-consent, protocol deviation assessment, or updated procedures for ongoing participants.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date on which the protocol amendment was formally submitted to the primary health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA). Marks the start of the regulatory review clock.']
  submission_reference_number varchar [note: 'Official reference number assigned by the health authority upon receipt of the amendment submission (e.g., FDA IND amendment serial number, EMA submission tracking number). Used for all subsequent regulatory correspondence.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this protocol amendment record, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  urgent_safety_measure_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this amendment was implemented as an urgent safety measure prior to regulatory approval, as permitted under GCP and EU CTR for immediate risk mitigation. Requires retrospective notification to health authorities.']
  veeva_vault_document_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in Veeva Vault eTMF/regulatory binder for the amendment package. Provides direct traceability to the source document management system of record.']

  Note: 'Tracks protocol amendments submitted to health authorities and ethics committees. Captures amendment number, amendment type (substantial/non-substantial), amendment rationale, affected study sections, submission date to each agency, agency acknowledgment date, approval date, implementation date, and impact on ongoing subjects. Links to the parent application and study protocol. Managed via Veeva Vault regulatory binder.'
}

  overall_completeness_status varchar [note: 'Aggregate readiness assessment of the entire CTD dossier across all five modules. Used for dossier gap analysis and submission readiness reviews.']
  planned_submission_date date [note: 'Target date on which the CTD dossier is planned to be submitted to the regulatory agency. Used for milestone tracking and resource planning.']
  prior_submission_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number of the prior submission or dossier version that this submission amends or supplements. Enables lineage tracking across submission cycles.']
  publishing_tool varchar [note: 'Name and version of the publishing software used to compile and validate the eCTD dossier (e.g., Lorenz docuBridge, Extedo eCTD Manager, Veeva Vault RIM Publisher). Critical for reproducibility and troubleshooting.']
  publishing_tool_version varchar [note: 'Version number of the publishing tool used to compile this dossier. Required for audit trail and reproducibility of the eCTD package.']
  sponsor_name varchar [note: 'Name of the pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor organization that owns the regulatory application and CTD dossier.']
  total_document_count varchar [note: 'Total number of individual content units (documents, datasets, study reports) included in this CTD dossier version. Used for completeness tracking and submission package verification.']
  validation_report_date date [note: 'Date on which the most recent eCTD technical validation report was generated for this dossier.']
  validation_report_status varchar [note: 'Status of the eCTD technical validation report generated by the publishing tool. Agencies require a passing validation report before accepting eCTD submissions.']
  veeva_vault_binder_reference varchar [note: 'Identifier of the Veeva Vault submission binder that organizes all CTD documents for this dossier. Enables navigation of the dossier structure within Veeva Vault.']
  veeva_vault_dossier_reference varchar [note: 'Unique document identifier assigned by Veeva Vault RIM to the CTD dossier record. Used for cross-system traceability between the lakehouse and the Veeva Vault eTMF/regulatory submissions system.']

  Note: 'Master record for the Common Technical Document (CTD) dossier structure and content inventory associated with a regulatory application. Tracks CTD format (eCTD/NeeS/paper), dossier version, completeness status, module-level readiness (Modules 1-5), last compiled date, validation report status, publishing tool used, and archival location in Veeva Vault. Also manages individual content units (documents, datasets, study reports) with CTD section references (e.g., Module 2.7.3, Module 5.3.5.1), document metadata, file format, lifecycle operations, and Veeva Vault document IDs. Serves as the structural backbone for all submission content and enables dossier gap analysis.'
}

  rolling_review_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the health authority has granted rolling review, allowing submission and review of completed CTD modules before the full dossier is complete. Applicable to FDA (Fast Track) and EMA rolling review procedures.']

  submission_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction where the application was submitted (e.g., USA, GBR, JPN, CAN, AUS). Supports multi-regional regulatory tracking.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date on which the complete application dossier was formally submitted to the health authority. Triggers the regulatory review clock and PDUFA goal date calculation.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Clinical therapeutic area or disease area for which the drug or biologic is being developed (e.g., oncology, cardiovascular, infectious disease, neurology). Used for portfolio management and regulatory strategy alignment.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this NDA/BLA application record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for change tracking and audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']

Populated when regulatory_action_required is True.']
  regulatory_action_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this safety report submission has triggered or requires a regulatory action such as a protocol amendment, IB update, informed consent revision, or clinical hold. Supports inspection readiness and CAPA tracking.']
  report_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the safety report being submitted. IND_SAFETY_REPORT = expedited IND safety report (15-day/7-day); DSUR = Development Safety Update Report; PSUR_PBRER = Periodic Safety Update Report / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report; SUSAR = Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction; IND_ANNUAL_REPORT = annual IND progress report; CIOMS = Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences line listing.']
  report_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the safety report document (e.g., 1.0, 2.0, 1.1 for amendments). Tracks original submissions versus follow-up or amended versions submitted to the same agency.']
  reporting_period_end_date date [note: 'End date of the data collection period covered by this safety report, also known as the data lock point (DLP). Defines the cut-off date for safety data included in the report.']
  reporting_period_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the data collection period covered by this safety report (e.g., the beginning of the DSUR or PSUR/PBRER data lock window). Applicable to periodic reports; may be null for expedited reports.']
  seriousness_criteria varchar [note: 'ICH E2A seriousness criterion that triggered the expedited reporting obligation for this submission. Applicable to SUSAR and IND safety reports. FATAL = resulted in death; LIFE_THREATENING = immediately life-threatening; HOSPITALIZATION = required or prolonged inpatient hospitalization; DISABILITY = persistent or significant disability/incapacity; CONGENITAL_ANOMALY = congenital anomaly/birth defect; MEDICALLY_SIGNIFICANT = other medically important condition.']
  submission_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction to which the safety report is submitted (e.g., USA, GBR, JPN, CAN, AUS). Supports multi-country submission tracking.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this safety report submission record. Supports audit trail integrity and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ requirements.']
  veeva_vault_document_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in Veeva Vault (eTMF/regulatory submissions module) for the finalized safety report document. Enables direct traceability from this submission record to the source document in the system of record.']

  Note: 'Tracks regulatory safety report submissions including IND Annual Reports, Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs), Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs/PBRERs), and expedited SUSAR/IND safety reports. Captures report type, reporting period, submission due date, actual submission date, agency acknowledgment, report version, and link to the source safety data. Distinct from individual AE/SAE records owned by the safety domain.'
}

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this submission content unit record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking and data integrity auditing.']
  validation_error_message varchar [note: 'Descriptive error or warning message returned by the eCTD validation tool or agency gateway when validation_status is \'failed\' or \'warning\'. Used for remediation and resubmission planning.']

  priority_designation varchar [note: 'Agency-specific priority or expedited designation granted or planned for this program at this authority (e.g., Breakthrough Therapy Designation at FDA, PRIME at EMA, Sakigake at PMDA, Promising Innovative Medicine at MHRA). Distinct from the boolean flags on clinical_program which are FDA/EMA-specific.']

  start_date date [note: 'Date on which the regulatory engagement with this authority for this program was formally initiated (e.g., first pre-IND meeting, first CTA submission, first scientific advice request).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract/Strategy between a clinical_program and a health_authority. It captures the agency-specific regulatory engagement plan for a given clinical development program — including submission strategy, target dates, regulatory pathway, and priority designations that are unique to each program-authority pairing. Each record links one health_authority to one clinical_program with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship and cannot reside on either master entity alone.. Existence Justification: In clinical research, a single clinical program (e.g., an oncology asset targeting multiple markets) is actively submitted to multiple health authorities simultaneously — FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA — each with its own submission strategy, regulatory pathway, target dates, and interaction plan. Conversely, each health authority oversees many clinical programs from many sponsors. The business actively manages this relationship as a named operational concept: a \'Regulatory Submission Strategy\' or \'Program-Agency Engagement\', with agency-specific data (submission dates, pathways, priority designations) that belongs to neither entity alone.'
}

Table regulatory.protocol_ethics_coverage {
  protocol_ethics_coverage_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the protocol_ethics_coverage association']
  ethics_submission_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the ethics submission package submitted to the IRB/IEC for this IND protocol']
  ind_application_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the IND application whose authorized protocol is covered by this ethics submission']
  ethics_committee_name varchar [note: 'The name of the IRB or IEC that received this ethics submission in the context of this IND protocol coverage. Retained at the association level to support regulatory reporting that maps IND protocols to specific reviewing ethics committees.']
  ind_serial_number varchar [note: 'The specific IND serial number (amendment sequence number) referenced by this ethics submission. Ethics submissions for protocol amendments reference the corresponding IND amendment serial number, enabling traceability between regulatory filings and ethics review packages.']
  protocol_number varchar [note: 'The protocol number identifying the specific clinical study protocol within the IND application that this ethics submission covers. A single IND may authorize multiple protocols; this attribute identifies which one is the subject of the ethics submission.']
  protocol_version varchar [note: 'The version identifier of the protocol document included in this ethics submission package as it relates to the IND. Captures which version of the IND-authorized protocol was submitted for IRB/IEC review in this specific linkage.']
  submission_date date [note: 'The date on which this ethics submission was transmitted to the IRB/IEC in the context of this specific IND protocol linkage. Retained at the association level to support timeline analysis across IND-ethics coverage records independently of the ethics_submission master record.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory-compliance contract between an IND application and an ethics submission. It captures which specific protocol (by number and version) under a given IND application is covered by a given IRB/IEC ethics submission, including the IND serial number amendment referenced. Each record links one ind_application to one ethics_submission and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this protocol-level regulatory linkage — enabling sponsors and regulatory teams to answer \'which ethics submissions cover which IND protocols?\' and \'which IND serial numbers are referenced by this ethics submission?\'. Existence Justification: In clinical trials, a single IND application covers multiple protocols, each of which requires its own ethics submission to an IRB/IEC — so one IND application is associated with many ethics submissions. Conversely, a single ethics submission (particularly an amendment or continuing review) may reference multiple IND serial numbers or cover protocols under different IND applications, meaning one ethics submission can be associated with multiple IND applications. The business actively tracks which ethics submissions are linked to which IND protocols/serial numbers as part of regulatory compliance management, and this linkage carries its own data (protocol number, protocol version, IND serial number, submission date, ethics committee name).'
}

  country_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the primary country or market for which this labeling document version applies (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU, JPN, CAN, AUS). Supports multi-regional labeling lifecycle management. [Moved from labeling_document: labeling_document.country_code represents the country for which a label is approved — this is a property of the approval relationship (which country approved this version), not of the document itself. A single document version may be approved in multiple countries; storing country_code on the document creates a 1:1 assumption that is architecturally incorrect.]']
  current_approved_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this record represents the currently active and approved labeling document version for this country registration. Only one record per country_registration should have this flag set to true at any point in time.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which this labeling document version became officially effective for this specific country registration. Differs per country as each health authority issues its own effective date. Belongs to the approval relationship, not to the document or registration alone.']
  health_authority_approval_date date [note: 'The date on which the health authority for this country formally approved this labeling document version for this registration. Country-specific — the same document version may be approved on different dates in different countries.']
  labeling_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the currently approved product labeling (SmPC, Package Insert, or equivalent) in this country. Tracks which labeling version is in force and supports variation management. [Moved from country_registration: country_registration.labeling_version is a denormalized string capturing the currently approved label version for this registration. This relationship data belongs in the label_approval association as a proper FK to labeling_document, with full history. The string field should be removed once the association table is in place.]']
  superseded_date date [note: 'The date on which this labeling document version was superseded by a newer approved version for this country registration. Null if this version is still the currently approved label in this country.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal approval event between a labeling_document version and a country_registration. It captures the regulatory act by which a health authority approves a specific labeling document version as the valid label for a product registration in a given country. Each record links one labeling_document to one country_registration and carries the country-specific approval status, effective dates, and health authority decision data that exist only in the context of this country-level label approval — not on the document or registration alone.. Existence Justification: In global regulatory affairs, a single labeling document (e.g., a Core Company Data Sheet or SmPC) is formally approved and in effect across multiple country registrations simultaneously, each with its own approval date, effective date, and status. Conversely, a single country registration tracks multiple labeling document versions over its lifecycle as the label is updated through variations and renewals. The business actively manages which specific label version is approved in each country — this is a recognized operational process called \'label approval\' or \'labeling registration\' in global regulatory operations.'
}

Table regulatory.binder_document_inclusion {
  binder_document_inclusion_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the binder_document_inclusion association']
  labeling_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the labeling document version included in this binder submission.']
  regulatory_binder_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the regulatory binder or eCTD submission package that contains this document.']
  ctd_section_code varchar [note: 'The specific CTD/eCTD module and section reference where this labeling document is filed within this particular binder (e.g., m1.3.1 for USPI in an NDA). Belongs to the inclusion relationship because the same document may be filed under different CTD sections in different binders.']
  inclusion_type varchar [note: 'Describes how the labeling document is included in the binder — e.g., ORIGINAL (full document), REFERENCE (hyperlinked reference to previously submitted document), AMENDMENT (revised version replacing prior inclusion). Belongs to the relationship as the same document can be included differently across binders.']
  is_mandatory boolean [note: 'Indicates whether inclusion of this labeling document is required by regulation or agency guidance for this specific binder type and submission. A document may be mandatory in an NDA original but optional in a supplement, making this an attribute of the inclusion relationship rather than the document itself.']
  language_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 639-1 language code of the labeling document as included in this specific binder. Captured at the inclusion level because a binder may include the same document type in multiple languages, and the language context of inclusion may differ from the document\'s primary language attribute.']
  redaction_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this labeling document requires redaction of confidential commercial information (CCI) for this particular submission and target agency. Redaction requirements vary by agency and submission type, making this an attribute of the inclusion relationship rather than the document itself.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the inclusion contract between a labeling_document and a regulatory_binder. It captures the operational act of assembling a regulatory submission binder by including specific labeling document versions, recording where each document is filed within the CTD structure, whether inclusion is mandatory, and any submission-specific handling requirements such as redaction. Each record links one labeling_document to one regulatory_binder with attributes that exist only in the context of this inclusion relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical regulatory operations, a labeling document (e.g., a USPI or SmPC) is genuinely included in multiple regulatory binders — the original NDA submission, subsequent supplements, annual reports, and amendments — while each binder contains multiple labeling documents covering different languages, CTD modules, and document types. This is an operationally managed relationship: regulatory affairs teams actively assemble binders by selecting and including specific labeling document versions, tracking which documents are mandatory, their CTD section placement, and whether redaction is required. The relationship is a recognized business concept in regulatory document management, commonly called a \'Binder Inclusion\' or \'Document Inclusion\'.'
}

  citation_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this ethics approval citation within the dossier: active (currently included), superseded (replaced by a newer ethics approval version), or withdrawn (removed from the dossier). Belongs to the citation relationship, not to either entity alone.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal inclusion of an ethics approval record within an NDA/BLA (or equivalent) application dossier. It captures the regulatory affairs act of citing a specific IRB/IEC ethics approval as supporting evidence within a marketing authorization application, including the CTD module where it is filed, the rationale for its inclusion, and the scope of the approval as it applies to the application. Each record links one nda_bla_application to one ethics_approval with attributes that exist only in the context of this dossier-level citation relationship.. Existence Justification: In clinical trials regulatory submissions, an NDA/BLA application dossier is built from evidence across multiple clinical studies, each of which has its own IRB/IEC ethics approval — so one application references many ethics approvals. Conversely, a pivotal study\'s ethics approval (e.g., a Phase III trial) can be cited in both an original NDA and a subsequent supplemental NDA (sNDA) or even a related BLA, meaning one ethics approval supports multiple applications. The business actively manages this linkage as part of dossier assembly, tracking which ethics approvals are included in which CTD module and why.'
}

Table regulatory.substantial_modification_submission {
  substantial_modification_submission_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the substantial_modification_submission association']
  clinical_trial_authorization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Clinical Trial Authorization held by the national competent authority receiving this substantial modification submission.']
  regulatory_protocol_amendment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the protocol amendment that is being submitted as a substantial modification to the competent authority.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the national competent authority formally approved this substantial modification submission. Null if decision is pending or negative.']
  decision_outcome varchar [note: 'Formal outcome of the national competent authority\'s review of this substantial modification submission. Each member state issues an independent decision; this attribute captures the country-specific result.']
  member_state_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code identifying the EU member state or non-EU jurisdiction whose competent authority is receiving this substantial modification submission. Denormalized here for query convenience alongside the CTA FK.']
  modification_scope varchar [note: 'Brief narrative description of the scope of the substantial modification as presented to this specific national competent authority. May differ slightly from the global amendment rationale to address country-specific regulatory requirements or language.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date on which this protocol amendment was formally submitted as a substantial modification to the national competent authority associated with this CTA. Distinct from the protocol_amendment.submission_date, which captures the primary authority submission date only.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory submission event between a protocol_amendment and a clinical_trial_authorization. It captures the per-member-state, per-amendment submission workflow required under EU CTR 536/2014 and equivalent national frameworks, where each protocol amendment must be formally submitted to and approved by each national competent authority holding a CTA for the trial. Each record links one protocol_amendment to one clinical_trial_authorization and carries the country-specific submission date, approval date, decision outcome, and modification scope that exist only in the context of this specific amendment-to-authority submission.. Existence Justification: Under EU CTR 536/2014, every substantial protocol amendment must be submitted as a separate modification to each national competent authority\'s CTA in each member state where the trial is running. A single protocol amendment (e.g., AM-003) generates distinct CTA modification submissions to Germany, France, Spain, etc., each with its own submission date, approval date, decision outcome, and member-state-specific conditions. Conversely, a single CTA accumulates multiple substantial modifications over the trial lifecycle as successive protocol amendments are approved. This is a genuine operational M:N: the business actively creates, tracks, and queries each amendment-to-CTA submission as a named regulatory workflow record.'
}

Existence Justification: In eCTD regulatory submissions, a single content unit (document/dataset) can legitimately appear across multiple regulatory binders — for example, a clinical study report submitted in an original NDA binder (sequence 0000) and then referenced again in a resubmission binder (sequence 0001) or a supplemental binder.
